N5 Grammar

と (With)

Polite

Good Morning Call · Episode 11

私わたしと付つき合あってください！

"Please go out with me!"

と after a person means "with": the person you do the action together with. It goes right after them: 私 + と.

On this card, it answers "Go out with who?": with me. The verb 付き合う ("go out, date") comes right after.

Between two nouns と means "and" (ヨーロッパと南米). With a verb after it, it's "with". Same in polite and casual speech.

Casual

Weakest Beast · Episode 5

私わたしは 克己さんと一緒いっしょにいたい。

"I want to be with Katsumi."

と after a person means "with". On this card, 克己さん + と + 一緒に + いたい ("want to be") = "want to be with Katsumi".

Examples

Someone asks who you went to the concert with.

姉あねと行いった。

"I went with my sister."

Casual

Saturday plans.

友達ともだちと映画えいがを見みます。

"I'm watching a movie with a friend."

Polite

Asking a coworker to lunch.

私わたしと一緒いっしょに食たべませんか？

"Want to eat with me?"

一緒に (together) after と makes the "with" extra clear. Very common.

Polite

With and without

Without

京都きょうとに行いきました。

I went to Kyoto. Maybe alone, we don't know.

With と

母ははと京都きょうとに行いきました。

I went to Kyoto with my mom. Now we know who came along.

Polite

僕ぼくと結婚けっこんしてください

"Please marry me."

Literally "please marry with me": in Japanese you marry with someone, so 結婚する takes と.

Polite

Kekkon Dekinai Otoko · Episode 7

誰だれも あなたと結婚けっこんなんかしません

"Nobody's going to marry you."

あなた + と + 結婚する: marry (with) you. なんか adds "something like that", making it dismissive.

Polite

Quartet · Episode 1

音楽おんがくと一緒いっしょに暮くらしたいです

"I want to live with music."

音楽 + と一緒に: "together with music".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 4

あなたと行いきたい海辺うみべのドライブ

"The seaside drive I want to go on with you."

あなたと行きたい describes the drive: the one I want to go on with you.

Casual

Kotaro Lives Alone · Episode 7

僕ぼく ホントは みんなと一緒いっしょに遊あそびたいんだ

"I actually want to play with everyone."

みんな + と + 一緒に ("together") + 遊びたい ("want to play").

Casual

Samurai Champloo · Episode 8

私わたしと一緒いっしょに飲のまない？

"Won't you have a drink with me?"

私 + と + 一緒に ("together") + 飲まない？ ("won't you drink?").

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 17

パンダくんと一緒いっしょに撮とった写真しゃしん、初はじめてだよ！

N5 Grammar

と (Quotation)

Polite～と思います
Casual～と思う neutral
～って思う spoken, very common

Same meaning: quoting a thought. って is the spoken casual と.

Polite

YouTube · video

そうですね！本当ほんとうに、みんなのおかげだと思おもいます！

"Totally! I think it's really all thanks to everyone!"

と closes off what someone thinks or says. The thought goes first, then と, then 思う (think) or 言う (say): みんなのおかげだ + と + 思います.

On this card, it answers "What do you think?": that it's all thanks to everyone. After a noun or な-adjective, add だ before と (おかげだと). After a verb or い-adjective, just と (高いと思う).

と works in polite and casual speech. In casual talk it often turns into って (below).

Casual

YouTube · video

でも、なんか日本にほん人じんで、すごくありそうな考かんがえ方かただなって思おもいました。

"But I thought, that's such a Japanese way of thinking."

って is the casual と. Same job, same spot: thought + って + 思う. The thought here is 考え方だな, "what a (Japanese) way of thinking".

Examples

A friend asks about the new ramen place.

おいしいと思おもう。

"I think it's good."

Casual

Passing on what the teacher said.

先生せんせいは、明日あしたテストがあると言いいました。

"The teacher said there's a test tomorrow."

What was said goes before と, who said it goes up front with は.

Polite

Looking at dark clouds.

明日あしたは雨あめだと思おもいます。

"I think it'll rain tomorrow."

雨 is a noun, so だ comes before と. Same with な-adjectives: 静かだと思う.

Polite

Telling a friend why Tanaka-san isn't here.

田中たなかさん、来こないって言いってたよ。

"Tanaka-san said they're not coming."

Casual: って instead of と.

Casual

With and without

Without

雨あめです。

It's raining. A plain fact.

With と

雨あめだと思おもいます。

I think it's raining. Now it's just my guess: と wraps up "it's rain", 思います says I think it.

Sentence mining

Polite

NHK News Web Easy · article

気象きしょう庁ちょうは、建物たてものの外そとにいるのはとても危あぶないと言いいました。

"The weather agency said being outside a building is very dangerous."

Who said it: 気象庁は. What they said: everything up to と.

Polite

YouTube · video

皆みなさんが温泉おんせんの街まちに行いったら、温泉おんせん卵たまごがあると思おもいます。

"When you visit a hot spring town, I think you'll find onsen eggs."

と思います softens it: not a promise, just what I expect.

Polite

YouTube · video

多分たぶん見みやすいと思おもいます。

"I think it's probably easy to see."

多分 (probably) and と思います often team up.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 12

動物どうぶつとの結婚けっこん生活せいかつは、難むずかしいと思おもうよ。

"I think married life with an animal would be hard."

難しい is an い-adjective, so no だ: straight into と.

Casual

YouTube · video

別べつに、多た機能きのうなエアコンだと思おもわないんだよ。

"I don't think it's a particularly fancy air conditioner."

"I don't think": the negative goes on 思う (思わない), not on the thought.

Casual

YouTube · video

今いまの撃うたれたよね。パチンって言いったもんな。

"We just got shot, right? It went 'bang'."

Sounds get quoted too: パチンって言った, "it went pachin".

Casual

Source unknown No source

コンタクトなんか怖こわいって言いってたのに

"And you said contacts were scary..."

言ってた: "you were saying". のに adds "and yet (look at you now)".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 21

ムリだと思おもうんだよね。

"I just don't think it's possible."

Your thought, then と思う.

N5 Grammar

の (Possession)

Polite

YouTube · video

名古屋なごやは僕ぼくの地元じもとです。

"Nagoya is my hometown."

の links two nouns: the owner first, then the thing. 僕 + の + 地元: my hometown. Like "'s" in English, but always in that order.

On this card, it answers "Whose hometown?": mine. Without の, 僕 and 地元 would just sit next to each other with no link.

The same in polite and casual speech. 私の, 僕の, 俺の are simply how you say "my".

Casual

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 1

これ、お父ちちさんの手作てづくりだ。

"Dad made this himself."

の links the owner to the thing. On this card, お父さんの手作り is Dad's handmade thing, with casual だ at the end.

Examples

Showing a friend a photo on your phone.

これ、僕ぼくの犬いぬ。

"This is my dog."

Casual

An umbrella is left by the door at work.

これは田中たなかさんの傘かさですか？

"Is this Tanaka-san's umbrella?"

Polite

Telling someone where you're eating tonight.

友達ともだちのお母ははさんの店みせに行いく。

"I'm going to my friend's mom's shop."

You can chain の, just like 's 's in English.

Casual

With and without

Without

車くるまです。

"It's a car." Just what it is.

With の

僕ぼくの車くるまです。

"It's my car." Now you know whose.

Polite

YouTube · video

火星かせいのお菓子かしです。

"Sweets from Mars."

火星のお菓子: Mars's sweets. の works for places too, not just people.

Polite

僕ぼくの息子むすこは最近さいきんよくハイハイします。

"My son has been crawling a lot lately."

Whose son? Mine: 僕の息子.

Polite

YouTube · video

長崎ながさき県けんの食たべ物ものです。

"It's a food from Nagasaki."

Place + の + noun: Nagasaki's food, food from Nagasaki.

Casual

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 1

中学ちゅうがくのバスケ部ぶの後輩こうはい

"A kid from my middle school basketball club."

Two の in a row: middle school's basketball club's junior. Each の hangs the next noun on the one before.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 9

フランスの古ふるい格言かくげんだよ

"It's an old French saying."

フランス + の = "France's", a saying from France.

Casual

N5 Grammar

の (Noun left out)

の after a person means "'s" or "my": 私の傘, "my umbrella". When everyone already knows which thing you mean, just drop it: 私の傘 → 私の, "mine".

The question works the same way: 誰の？, "whose?". Polite or casual only shows at the end: 私のです / 私のだ / just 私の.

Examples

An umbrella was left in the office kitchen. Someone holds it up.

A: この傘かさ、誰だれのですか。
B: あ、私わたしのです。

A: "Whose umbrella is this?" B: "Oh, it's mine."

The umbrella is right there, so B doesn't need to say 傘 again.

Polite

A coworker finds a key on the desk.

その鍵かぎ、田中たなかさんのですよ。

"That key is Tanaka's."

Works with names too: 田中さんの = "Tanaka's".

Polite

Your little brother reaches for the last pudding in the fridge.

それ、私わたしの！

"That's mine!"

Casual

A phone rings on the table. Your friend looks at you.

俺おれのじゃないよ。

"It's not mine."

Negative: 俺の + じゃない.

Casual

With and without

Without

これは私わたしの本ほんです。

"This is my book." You name the thing.

With の alone

これは私わたしのです。

"This is mine." The book is right there, so you leave it out.

Polite

"It's yours."

Something is held out: あなたの = "yours".

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 6

私の + じゃない = "not mine".

"Oh, that's mine."

A phone buzzes. 私の = "my phone", without saying phone.

みかん詰つめ詰づめゼリーは 僕ぼくのだろうが

"That mandarin jelly is mine!"

僕の = "mine". だろうが here is an annoyed "obviously".

Casual

"This is yours, right?"

お前の = "yours" (rough, boyish). He's handing back her lunch box.

"Then whose is it?"

誰の？ = "whose?". The thing is already clear, so it's left out.

"It's mine after all, right?"

僕の = mine, the noun is left out.

N5 Grammar

から

Polite

Comprehensible Japanese · これ、それ、あれ、どれ

松まつぼっくりは、松まつの木きからおちます。

"Pine cones fall from pine trees."

から means from. It marks the starting point, and it goes right after it: 松の木 + から = "from the pine tree".

On this card, the pine cone starts up in the tree and ends on the ground. The sentence answers "Where do they fall from?": the tree.

から is the same in polite and casual speech. The politeness comes from the end: おちます here, おちる with friends.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 6

昔むかしから、マイペースだよな、お前まえは

"You've always done things at your own pace, haven't you."

から works for time too: 昔 + から = "from long ago", so "always". Casual, so だよな instead of ですね.

Examples

A new coworker asks where you're from.

ドイツから来きました。

"I came from Germany."

Place + から: where you started.

Polite

Someone asks when the shop opens.

十じゅう時じからです。

"From ten o'clock."

Time + から: when something starts.

Polite

Your friend shows you a new sweater.

お母ははさんからもらった。

"I got it from my mom."

Person + から: who it came from.

Casual

You're about to start cleaning a messy room.

どこからやろう？

"Where should I start?"

Literally "from where should I do it?"

Casual

With and without

Without

駅えきに歩あるきました。

"I walked to the station." The station is where you ended up.

With から

駅えきから歩あるきました。

"I walked from the station." The station is where you started.

Sentence mining

Polite

"The number of people getting mycoplasma pneumonia has kept rising since last month."

先月 + から = "since last month". With time, "from" often becomes "since" in English.

"The next day, early in the morning, we head from Nagoya to Osaka in this car again."

名古屋から = the start, 大阪に = the goal.

たった週しゅう2回かいのバイトなのに、朝あさから居眠いねむりしないでよ。

"You only work twice a week, so don't nod off [starting right] from the morning."

朝から: the day has barely started and he's already asleep.

Casual

Pokémon: Indigo League · Episode 3

よ～し、これからビシバシゲットしていくぜ！

"Alright, from now on I'm gonna catch them like crazy!"

これから = "from now on". A very common pair, worth learning as one word.

Casual

おっ、晶ちゃんから返事へんじ来きた！

"Oh! Akira replied!"

晶ちゃん + から ("from") + 返事 ("a reply") + 来た ("came") = "a reply came from Akira".

Casual

今いまね、教室きょうしつから帰かえってきたばっかり。

"I just got back from class."

教室 ("class, lesson room") + から + 帰ってきた ("came back") = "got back from class". ばっかり: "just now".

Spirited Away

あなたは どこから来きたの？

"Where did you come from?"

どこ + から + 来た ("came") = "where did you come from?". の makes it a soft question.

N5 Grammar

まで

Polite

YouTube · video

でも、昔むかしの侍さむらいは東京とうきょうから京都きょうとまで歩あるいたらしいです。

"But back then, samurai apparently walked all the way from Tokyo to Kyoto."

まで means until, up to, as far as. It marks the end point, and it goes right after it: 京都 + まで = "as far as Kyoto".

It often teams up with から (from): 東京から京都まで = "from Tokyo to Kyoto". On this card, the sentence answers "How far did they walk?": all the way to Kyoto.

まで is the same in polite and casual speech. The politeness comes from the end: らしいです here, らしい with friends.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 1

何なん時じまで寝ねてるの

"How long are you going to sleep?"

まで works for time too: 何時 + まで = "until when". Casual, so just の at the end instead of んですか.

Examples

A friend asks about your work hours.

九きゅう時じから五ご時じまで働はたらきます。

"I work from nine to five."

Time + まで: when something stops.

Polite

The bus isn't coming and the station is close.

駅えきまで歩あるこう。

"Let's walk to the station."

Place + まで: how far you go.

Casual

Your friend is still finishing their homework.

終おわるまで待まつよ。

"I'll wait until you're done."

Verb (dictionary form) + まで: until that thing happens.

Casual

Your joke was so silly that the strict teacher laughed too.

先生せんせいまで笑わらった！

"Even the teacher laughed!"

Person or thing + まで can also mean even: it goes "as far as" the one you'd least expect.

Casual

With and without

Without

七なな時じに寝ねます。

"I go to sleep at seven." に is one point in time: when it starts.

With まで

七なな時じまで寝ねます。

"I sleep until seven." まで is where the sleeping ends.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

宅たく急便きゅうびんの人ひとが、自分じぶんの家いえまで届とどけてくれるじゃないですか。

"The delivery person brings it all the way to your house, right?"

自分の家まで: the package goes as far as your own door.

15日にちは、北海道ほっかいどうから九州きゅうしゅうまでの多おおくの場所ばしょで、気温きおんが上あがりました。

"On the 15th, temperatures rose in many places from Hokkaido to Kyushu."

北海道から九州まで: top to bottom of Japan. まで + の works like an adjective: "the places from Hokkaido to Kyushu".

YouTube · video

下したまで押おしてったら、あのリールを巻まく。

"Once you've pushed it all the way down, you wind that reel."

下まで = "to the bottom". Not just down a bit, all the way.

Casual

YouTube · video

でも、手前てまえに1人ひとりいるぐらいか。こっちの家いえまで、引ひっ張ぱってこれればいいんだけどな。

"But there's maybe just one in front. I wish I could lure it over to this house."

こっちの家まで: the goal is to get it as far as this house.

Smoking · Episode 12

最後さいごまで 一緒いっしょにいたい。

"I want to be with you until the end."

最後 ("the end") + まで = "until the end". 一緒にいたい: "I want to be together".

Casual

Border · Episode 3

最後さいごまで信しんじてくれないか？

"Won't you trust me to the end?"

最後 ("the end") + まで + 信じて ("believe") = "believe me to the end". くれないか: "won't you?".

Steins Gate · Episode 15

あしたまでには なんとか。

"Somehow, by tomorrow."

あした ("tomorrow") + までに = "by tomorrow". まで is "until", までに is "by" a deadline.

"I'll take you home."

N5 Grammar

には・では・にも

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 38

春はるにはお花見はなみしましたよね

"[And] in spring, we went to see the cherry blossoms, right?"

A word in a sentence usually already has a particle after it: 魚を, 春に, 家で. Sometimes you also want も ("too") or は ("as for...") on that same word. So what happens to the particle that was already there?

  • を and が go away. も or は takes their place.
    魚さかなを食たべた → 魚さかなも食たべた "I ate fish too." Never をも.
  • に stays. も or は goes right after it.
    春はるに → 春はるには / 春はるにも "in spring" / "in spring too"
  • で stays too. Same thing.
    家いえで → 家いえでは / 家いえでも "at home" / "at home too"

Why: を and が only point at who does it and to what. も and は can do that job by themselves. に and で mean something (in, at, to), so they can't go.

On this card, they're looking back on the year. 春に is "in spring", and は makes it the topic: "as for spring, we went flower viewing."

Casual

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 6

私わたしにも見みせて。

"Show me too."

On this card, he's looking at plankton and she wants a look too. 見せて is "show", 私に is "to me", and も goes after に: "to me too".

Examples

A friend asks how your trip to Kyoto and Osaka went.

京都きょうとには行いったけど、大阪おおさかには行いかなかった。

"I went to Kyoto, but not to Osaka."

に (to) stays. は sets the two cities side by side.

Casual

A new coworker asks if you speak English at the office.

会社かいしゃでは日本語にほんごを話はなします。

"At work, I speak Japanese."

で (at) stays. は adds "at work, anyway": maybe not at home.

Polite

Back from a trip, you hand out souvenirs and remember one more person.

山田やまださんにもお土産みやげを買かいました。

"I bought a souvenir for Yamada-san too."

に (for) stays, も goes after it.

Polite

You already had a big lunch, and then someone brought cake.

ケーキも食たべた。

"I ate cake too."

ケーキを食べた, but を disappears: never ケーキをも.

Casual

With and without

Without に

田中たなかさんも話はなした。

"Tanaka talked too." Tanaka is the one talking.

With に

田中たなかさんにも話はなした。

"I told Tanaka too." Tanaka is the one being told. Drop に and the meaning changes.

Sentence mining

Polite

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 3

先生せんせいには分わかりません。

"You wouldn't understand, Doctor."

A mother to a young doctor. 分かる uses に for who understands: 先生に + は. "You, unlike a parent."

Polite

Slam Dunk · Episode 16

素人しろうとには見みえませんよ

"He doesn't look like a beginner."

に見える is "look like". に stays, は goes after it.

Polite

Kekkon Dekinai Otoko · Episode 4

このことは誰だれにも秘密ひみつですよ

"This is a secret from everyone, okay?"

誰に + も: "to anyone". 秘密 here means "not telling".

Casual

Kekkon Dekinai Otoko · Episode 4

英治えいじにも教おしえてないんで

"I haven't even told Eiji."

教える uses に for who you tell: 英治に + も. With a negative, も means "not even".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 12

家いえにもたくさんあるんだけど

"I've got lots at home too, but..."

Talking about a collection. ある uses に for where: 家に + も.

Casual

Kotaro Lives Alone · Episode 3

ほれ　俺おれにも撮とらせろ

"Here, let me take one too."

She's taking photos and he wants a turn. 撮らせろ is a rough "let me take": 俺に + も.

Casual

Slam Dunk · Episode 97

選抜せんばつでは　絶対ぜったいに負まけない

"At the Winter Cup, we won't lose."

選抜 is the winter tournament. で + は: "at that one, unlike this time".

Casual

JoJo's Bizarre Adventure · Episode 26

ただ　太陽たいようの下したでは走はしれない

"But he couldn't run under the sun."

A man who could do anything, except this. 下で + は: anywhere else yes, under the sun no.

N5 Grammar

だけ

Polite

YouTube · video

夢ゆめ応援おうえん面談めんだん　聞きくのは３つだけです

"The Dream Support Interview: I only ask three questions."

だけ means only, just. It goes right after the thing you're limiting: ３つ + だけ = "only three".

On this card: no fourth question, no follow-ups. He's saying it's that simple. It answers "How many questions?": just three.

だけ is the same in polite and casual speech. The politeness comes from the end: だけです here, just だけ with friends.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 5

間違まちがいはないけど、フェアなのに定番ていばんだけじゃつまらない。

"They're a safe choice, but for a special menu, [having] only the usual ones is boring."

定番 + だけ = "only the usual ones". Casual, so no です at the end.

Examples

At the café, the waiter asks what you'd like.

コーヒーだけお願ねがいします。

"Just a coffee, please."

Noun + だけ. No cake, no sandwich, only coffee.

Polite

Someone asks if you speak lots of languages.

英語えいごと日本にほん語ごだけです。

"Only English and Japanese."

だけ can cover a whole list: 英語と日本語 + だけ.

Polite

Your friend offers you more snacks.

一いち個こだけちょうだい。

"Just give me one."

Number + だけ: only one, not more.

Casual

Your friend asks what you did on Sunday.

家いえで寝ねてただけ。

"I just slept at home."

Verb + だけ: that's all you did. The verb stays in its plain form (寝てた, 見る, 行った).

Casual

With and without

Without

水みずを飲のみました。

"I drank water." Maybe you had other things too.

With だけ

水みずだけ飲のみました。

"I only drank water." Nothing else. を often drops out after だけ.

Sentence mining

Polite

Comprehensible Japanese · My Five Favorite Things

でも、昔むかしのキンドルは少すこしだけ凹へこんでいます。

"But on the old Kindle, the screen is just a little sunken in."

少し + だけ = "just a little". だけ makes 少し even smaller.

Polite

Weakest Beast · Episode 9

あとは 出だすだけです。

"All that's left is to hand it in."

あとは ("the rest is") + 出す ("hand in") + だけ: the only thing left is to hand it in.

Casual

YouTube · video

それは、０号ごう車しゃまで行いって、その先さきの運転うんてん室しつでブレーキをかけるだけ。

"That's just going to car 0 and hitting the brakes in the driver's cab past it."

Verb + だけ: that's all there is to do. ブレーキをかけるだけ = "just put on the brakes".

Casual

YouTube · video

二人ふたりの生活せいかつ費ひは月つき6万まん円えんほど、以前いぜんより2万まん円えん増ふえただけ。

"Living costs for the two of them are about 60,000 yen a month, only 20,000 more than before."

増えただけ: "only went up (by that much)". だけ makes the amount sound small.

Casual

Weakest Beast · Episode 3

それだけ？

"That's it?"

それ ("that") + だけ = "only that?". Said when you expected more.

Casual

Overprotected Kahoko · Episode 3

ただ… 悲かなしいだけ。

"I'm just... sad."

悲しい ("sad") + だけ = "just sad", nothing else. ただ adds "simply".

Casual

From the New World · Episode 10

10分ぷんだけだ。

"Just ten minutes."

10分 ("ten minutes") + だけ = "only ten minutes", not a minute more.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 28

1日いちにちだけだよ。

"Just for one day."

だけ comes right after what it limits.

N5 Grammar

しか～ない

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 2

パンダ君くんの好物こうぶつしかおいてないじゃない..　そのカフェ。

"That café only has Panda's favorite foods, doesn't it..."

しか means only, but the verb after it is always negative. It goes right after the thing you're limiting: パンダ君の好物 + しか.

On this card, the café keeps nothing but Panda's favorite foods: しか + おいてない (置いてない, "don't keep"). The じゃない at the end is "isn't it?", not part of しか.

しか always sounds like "that's all, and it's not much". In polite speech the end becomes ません: しかおいていません.

Polite

YouTube · video

これサンピン茶ちゃは沖縄おきなわでしか飲のむことができません。ま、多分たぶん名古屋なごやにもあるかな。

"This here, sanpin tea, you can only drink in Okinawa. Well, maybe Nagoya has it too."

Polite, so the negative is ません. Place + で + しか: "only in Okinawa". で stays, but を and が drop out before しか.

Examples

You check your wallet before paying.

500円えんしかありません。

"I only have 500 yen."

Not much money, and you're a bit worried. しか + ありません.

Polite

A coworker asks if you speak Chinese too.

日本にほん語ごと英語えいごしか話はなせません。

"I can only speak Japanese and English."

しか can cover a whole list: 日本語と英語 + しか.

Polite

Your friend opens your fridge, looking for food.

ビールしかないよ。

"There's nothing but beer."

ビールがない would be "there's no beer". With しか it flips: beer is the only thing there.

Casual

Your friend asks how many people came to the party.

三さん人にんしか来こなかった。

"Only three people came."

Past: しか + なかった. You hoped for more.

Casual

With and without

Without

三さん時間じかん寝ねた。

"I slept three hours." Just a fact.

With しか

三さん時間じかんしか寝ねてない。

"I only slept three hours." Not enough, and you feel it. Same as だけ in meaning, but だけ is neutral (三時間だけ寝た) and しか sounds like a complaint.

Polite

Border · Episode 3

50年ねんほどの歴史れきししかありません

"It only has about 50 years of history."

しか + ありません: "has nothing but 50 years". Polite negative.

世界せかいに４枚まいしかないうちの１枚まいじゃ、値段ねだんのつけようもないわい。

"It's one of only four in the world, so there's no way to put a price on it."

４枚しかない = "there are only four". Here it describes the cards: "the only-four-in-the-world ones".

君きみしかいないんだ。

"You're the only one."

君 ("you") + しか + いない ("isn't there") = "there's nobody but you", "you're the only one".

Casual

平日へいじつしか使つかえないんだ？

"So you can only use it on weekdays?"

平日 ("weekdays") + しか + 使えない ("can't use") = "can only use it on weekdays".

Casual

信しんじるしかないな。

"All we can do is trust her."

信じる ("believe") + しかない = "nothing to do but believe". Verb + しかない: it's the only option left.

Casual

Overprotected Kahoko · Episode 2

加か穂ほ子こにしかできないこと

"Something only Kahoko can do."

加穂子 + に ("for") + しか + できない ("can't do") = "something only Kahoko can do".

Casual

仲直なかなおりするしかないよ。

"We just have to make up."

仲直りする ("make up") + しかない = "we have no choice but to make up".

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 10

竹たけしか食たべてないから。

"Because I only eat bamboo."

しか needs a negative verb after it.

N5 Grammar

ぐらい・くらい

Polite

YouTube · video

フレーバーの紅茶こうちゃで、100種類しゅるいぐらいあるんですよ！

"There are about 100 kinds of flavored tea!"

ぐらい means about, roughly. It goes right after an amount: 100種類 + ぐらい = "about 100 kinds".

On this card, she didn't count them. ぐらい tells you the number is a rough guess. It answers "How many?": around 100.

くらい and ぐらい are the same word. Say whichever comes out, both are fine in polite and casual speech.

Casual

YouTube · video

最初さいしょの1時間じかんは無料むりょうなんだけど、それ以降いこうは1時間じかん100円えんくらい。

"The first hour is free, but after that it's about 100 yen an hour."

Same thing with くらい: 100円くらい = "about 100 yen". Casual, so no です at the end.

Examples

Someone asks how long you've studied Japanese.

3年ねんぐらいです。

"About three years."

Without ぐらい it's exactly three years. With it, "give or take".

Polite

Asking the hotel how far the station is.

駅えきまで歩あるいてどのくらいかかりますか？

"How long does it take to walk to the station?"

どの + くらい = "about how much?": the question version. どれくらい means the same. Answer: 10分ぐらいです.

Polite

Your friend is cooking rice and asks you.

ご飯はん、どれくらい食たべる？

"How much rice do you want?"

You can answer with your hands: このくらい. "About this much."

Casual

A friend asks how much your new bike cost.

5万まん円えんくらいかな。

"About 50,000 yen, I think."

くらい + かな: you're not quite sure of the price.

Casual

With and without

Without

駅えきまで10分ぷんかかります。

"It takes 10 minutes to the station." Sounds exact.

With ぐらい

駅えきまで10分ぷんぐらいかかります。

"It takes about 10 minutes to the station." A rough guess.

Sentence mining

Polite

Kiki's Delivery Service

40分ぷんくらいでしょうか。

"About 40 minutes, I'd say."

40分 ("40 minutes") + くらい + でしょうか ("I'd say"): a polite guess.

Polite

The Journalist · Episode 4

何なん人にんぐらい いるんですか？

"About how many people are there?"

何人 ("how many people") + ぐらい: asking for a rough number.

Casual

YouTube · video

ちょっと雪ゆきも降ふりました。ちょっとね。このぐらいかな。

"It snowed a little too. Just a bit. About this much, I guess."

このぐらい: "about this much", while showing it. Polite start, casual かな at the end.

Casual

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 10

35とか それぐらい。

"Around 35 or so."

35とか ("35 or so") + それ ("that") + ぐらい = "around that". Two ways of saying "roughly" at once.

Casual

Steins Gate · Episode 1

15分ふんくらい前まえ。

"About fifteen minutes ago."

15分 ("15 minutes") + くらい + 前 ("ago") = "about 15 minutes ago".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 15

20回かいくらい。

"About twenty times."

20回 ("20 times") + くらい = "about twenty times".

Casual

Overprotected Kahoko · Episode 7

まだって どれくらい？

""Not yet"? How long is that?"

どれ + くらい = "how much?", here "how long?". まだって: "you say 'not yet', but...".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 25

一いち週間しゅうかんに1回かいくらい。

"About once a week."

くらい comes after the amount.

Reference

A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

Entry "kurai" · pp. 212–213

N5 Grammar

ごろ (頃)

Casual

Midnight Diner (深夜食堂) · opening

営業えいぎょう時間じかんは夜よる12時じから、朝あさ7時じごろまで。

"My hours are from midnight until about seven in the morning." [the diner's opening hours]

ごろ means around, about, for a point in time. It goes right after the time: 7時 + ごろ = "around 7 o'clock".

On this card, midnight is a fixed time, so no ごろ. Seven is a rough end time, so it gets ごろ. It answers "When?": around seven.

Same word in polite and casual speech. In writing you'll also see it as 頃.

Polite

Million Yen Woman · Episode 7

何時なんじ頃ごろに帰かえってきますか？

"Around what time will he be home?" [a reporter asking]

ごろ goes right after a time and means "around". On this card, 何時 ("what time") + ごろ asks for a rough time, so "around 9" is a fine answer. ます makes the question polite.

Examples

A coworker asks when you'll get to the office.

9時じごろ着つきます。

"I'll get there around nine."

Some people add に: 9時ごろに着きます. Same meaning, with or without it.

Polite

Your friend asks when you went to bed.

2時じごろかな。

"Around two, I think."

Casual

Talking about when the cherry blossoms come out.

桜さくらは4月がつの初はじめごろです。

"The cherry blossoms are around early April."

Not only clock times: days, months and seasons work too.

Polite

Planning when to meet up.

じゃあ、6時じごろ駅えきで。

"Okay, at the station around six, then."

Casual

With and without

Without

7時じに起おきました。

"I got up at seven." Sounds exact.

With ごろ

7時じごろ起おきました。

"I got up around seven." A rough time.

ごろ or ぐらい?

ぐらい: how long

2時間じかんぐらい寝ねました。

"I slept for about two hours." An amount of time.

ごろ: when

2時じごろ寝ねました。

"I went to bed around two." A point in time.

Source unknown No source

7日なのかの午後ごご7時じ半はん頃ころ、群馬ぐんま県けん沼田ぬまた市しのスーパーに熊くまが出でました。

"Around 7:30 pm on the 7th, a bear showed up at a supermarket in Numata, Gunma."

News style: 頃 in kanji, right after the time.

Polite

Weakest Beast · Episode 10

深海ふかみさん 何時なんじごろ来きますか？

"Around what time is Shinkai coming?"

何時 ("what time") + ごろ = "around what time?".

Polite

Border · Episode 1

12時じごろから5時じごろまでです。

"From around 12 to around 5."

ごろ works with から and まで too.

Polite

Legal High · Episode 9

症状しょうじょうが出で始はじめたのは いつごろですか？

"Around when did the symptoms start?"

いつ ("when") + ごろ = "around when?". 症状が出始めた: "the symptoms started".

Casual

I am Mita, Your Housekeeper · Episode 9

今日きょう 帰かえり何時なんじごろ？

"Around what time are you coming home today?"

何時 ("what time") + ごろ = "around what time?". 帰り: "coming home". Casual: no です.

Casual

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 1

うん、3時じごろかな。

"Yeah, around 3, I think."

3時 ("3 o'clock") + ごろ = "around 3". かな: "I think".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 18

あれ？何時なんじ頃ごろに寝ねたんだっけ？

"Wait, around what time did I go to bed?"

頃 follows a time word.

Reference

A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

Entry "goro" · pp. 126–128

N5 Grammar

よ

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 8

取材しゅざいの人ひとですよ

"[Those people?] They're here for an interview, you know."

よ at the end of a sentence means "I'm telling you": you push what you're saying onto the listener. Sometimes it's news they don't know yet, sometimes it just adds weight: reassuring (いいですよ), insisting (信じてよ), firmly confirming (そうだよ). It goes on the very end, after です, ます or a plain verb or adjective.

On this card, the other person doesn't know who the visitors are. The speaker fills them in. Without よ, 取材の人です is just a flat fact; with よ it's "hey, here's the info you're missing".

Polite: ですよ / ますよ. Casual: drop です, but after a noun or な-adjective add だ: 取材の人だよ (取材の人よ without だ sounds feminine and old-fashioned)

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 2

お花見はなみらしくなってきたよ

"It's starting to look like a real hanami party!"

Here よ goes right after the plain verb. They're hanging up flags and sharing how it's coming along with everyone around them.

Examples

Your friend is about to leave without their phone. It's still on the table.

スマホ、忘わすれてるよ

"You're forgetting your phone!"

Casual

Your friend is trying to decide if the new ramen place is worth it. You've been.

あそこ、おいしいよ

"That place is good, trust me."

Casual

A customer is looking around for the bathroom. You work there.

トイレは二に階かいですよ

"The bathroom's upstairs."

Polite

A coworker is rushing to catch the 6:00 train. You know it was cancelled.

その電車でんしゃ、今日きょうは来きませんよ

"That train isn't coming today, just so you know."

Polite

With and without

Without

おいしい

"It's tasty." You're eating and just say it, to yourself or anyone.

With よ

おいしいよ

"It's tasty, try it!" You're telling someone who hasn't tried it.

Without

二に階かいです

"It's on the second floor." Neutral answer.

With よ

二に階かいですよ

"It's upstairs." Friendlier, you're helping them out.

Polite

YouTube · video

国際こくさい線せんですよ。

"This is the international terminal."

Telling the viewer something they might not know. よ after です.

Polite

Good Morning Call · Episode 6

忘わすれ物ものですよ

"You forgot something!"

The other person hasn't noticed they left something behind. よ hands them that news.

Polite

Kekkon Dekinai Otoko · Episode 9

あの人ひとですよ

"[Look,] that's the guy!"

She spots someone her friend hasn't noticed. よ points it out: "that's him, you didn't see?"

Casual

Kotaro Lives Alone · Episode 3

これからもずっと一緒いっしょだよ

"We'll always be together from now on."

一緒 is a noun, so casual needs だ before よ: 一緒だよ, not 一緒よ.

Casual

I am Mita, Your Housekeeper · Episode 3

そうだよ

"That's right."

そうだ + よ: adds weight, "yes, that's right!"

Casual

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 4

御飯ごはん出来できたよ

"Dinner's ready!"

Mom calls her daughter to eat. よ after the plain past: "hey, it's ready".

Adverbs and Sentence-ending particles · 「よ」 sentence ending

N5 Grammar

ね

Polite

YouTube · video

綺麗きれいな鳴なき声ごえですね

"[Hear that bird?] What a beautiful song, isn't it?"

ね at the end of a sentence means "you see it too, right?". It goes on the very end, after です, ます or a plain verb or adjective.

On this card, she's walking in the forest with her viewers, and they can all hear the bird. She isn't giving news, she's sharing the moment and inviting them to agree.

Polite: ですね / ますね. Casual: drop です, but after a noun or な-adjective add だ: 綺麗な鳴き声だね.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 5

楽たのしそうだね

"That sounds fun, huh."

そう ("looks like") works like a な-adjective, so it gets だ before ね.

Examples

You and a friend step outside. It's freezing.

寒さむいね

"It's cold, huh."

Casual

You're both eating the curry your friend made. It's really good.

これ、おいしいね

"This is good, isn't it."

Casual

Small talk with a neighbor while it pours outside.

よく降おりますね

"It sure is raining a lot."

Polite

A coworker shows you a photo of their new apartment.

広ひろい部屋へやですね

"What a big room."

Polite

With and without

Without

寒さむい

"It's cold." Just a statement, to yourself or anyone.

With ね

寒さむいね

"It's cold, huh." You both feel it, and you're sharing that.

With よ

寒さむいよ

"It's cold, you know." They don't know yet, so you tell them (maybe they're about to go out without a coat).

With ね

広ひろい部屋へやですね

"What a big room." You're both looking at it.

Polite

YouTube · video

やっぱり、日本にほんの方ほうが寒さむいですね。

"Japan really is colder, huh."

She's comparing two places and expects the listener to agree. ね after です.

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 15

遮光しゃこう器き土偶どぐうですね

"That's a dogū figurine, huh."

ですね: the polite version, both looking at the same thing.

Polite

Smoking · Episode 1

お目覚めざめですね

"Oh, you're awake."

ね: saying what you both can see.

Casual

Overprotected Kahoko · Episode 6

そうだね。

"Yeah."

そうだ ("that's right") + ね = "yeah, true". Agreeing and sharing the feeling.

Casual

Weakest Beast · Episode 5

幸しあわせだね

"You're so lucky."

Casual だ + ね.

Casual

Mob Psycho 100 · Episode 10

そうだね

"That's right."

Agreeing: "yeah, true".

Casual

The Journalist · Episode 3

そうだね

"You're right."

Same move: そうだ + ね, agreeing.

Adverbs and Sentence-ending particles · 「ね」 sentence ending

N5 Grammar

よね

Polite

YouTube · video

仙台せんだいには、国際こくさい空港くうこうもありますよね。

"[Talking about Sendai] Sendai has an international airport too, right?"

よね at the end of a sentence means "I'm pretty sure this is true, right?". It goes on the very end, after です, ます or a plain verb or adjective.

On this card, she knows Sendai has an airport, and she's checking that you're with her. It's not news (that's よ) and it's not something you're both looking at right now (that's ね): it's something she already believes and wants a nod on.

Polite: ですよね / ますよね. Casual: drop です, but after a noun or な-adjective add だ: 週二日だよね.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 14

パンダ君くんのバイトって、週しゅう二日ふつかだよね。

"Panda's part-time job is two days a week, right?"

He thinks he remembers, and he's double-checking. 週二日 is a noun, so it gets だ before よね.

Examples

You're meeting a friend tomorrow and want to make sure you have the time right.

明日あした、十じゅう時じだよね

"Tomorrow's at ten, right?"

Casual

Your friend says they hate waiting in long lines. You feel the same.

わかる。長ながい列れつ、嫌いやだよね

"I get it. Long lines are the worst, right?"

Casual

Not checking a fact here: you're agreeing, and saying "everyone feels this, don't they".

You're about to pay at a shop and want to check before you hand over your card.

カード、使つかえますよね

"I can use a card, right?"

Polite

A coworker mentioned last week they were from Osaka.

田中たなかさん、大阪おおさか出身しゅっしんですよね

"Tanaka-san, you're from Osaka, right?"

Polite

With and without

With よ

明日あした、十じゅう時じだよ

"Tomorrow's at ten, you know." You're telling them. They don't know yet.

With よね

明日あした、十じゅう時じだよね

"Tomorrow's at ten, right?" You think so, and you're checking with them.

With ね

寒さむいね

"It's cold, huh." You both feel it right now, and you're sharing that.

With よね

冬ふゆの北海道ほっかいどうって、寒さむいよね

"Hokkaido in winter is cold, right?" Not something you feel right now: something you're sure about and want them to agree with.

Polite

YouTube · video

えっと、皆みなさん、バベルの塔とうって知しってますよね？

"Um, everyone, you know the Tower of Babel, right?"

She assumes her viewers know it and checks before going on. ますよね: the polite version.

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 5

パフェフェアって、なんか言いいづらいですよね。

"'Parfait fair' is kind of hard to say, isn't it."

His own opinion, but he's sure the others will agree. ですよね after an い-adjective (polite).

Polite

Million Yen Woman · Episode 10

そうですよね

"Yes, that's right."

そうです + よね: agreeing and checking at the same time.

Casual

Teasing Master Takagi-san · Season 3, Episode 3

これってさ… 間接かんせつキス…だよね？

"Hey, this is... an indirect kiss... right?"

He's pretty sure, and needs her to confirm. 間接キス is a noun, so casual gets だよね.

Casual

New Atashin'chi · Episode 1

お母ははさん、新しん兵器へいき好すきだよねえ。

"Mom, you sure love your new gadgets, huh."

Something she's seen Mom do again and again. 好き is a な-adjective, so だよね. The long え just makes it sound more fed up.

Casual

Weakest Beast · Episode 5

そうだよね。

"Yeah, you're right."

そうだ ("that's right") + よね = "yeah, you're right". Agreeing, and checking you both see it the same way.

Casual

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 5

いいよね？

"It's OK, right?"

よね checks something you think the other person agrees with.

Tae Kim's Guide to Japanese Grammar

Adverbs and Sentence-ending particles · Combining both to get 「よね」

N5 Grammar

でしょう

Polite

He Who Can't Marry · Episode 1

開業かいぎょう資金しきんはうちの父ちちが貸かしてくれるでしょう。

"My dad will probably lend [us] the money to start the business."

でしょう means "probably": you think it's true, but you're not 100% sure. It goes at the very end, after a plain verb, an い-adjective, or a noun (no だ before it).

On this card, she answers "Where will the money come from?": her dad, most likely. Without でしょう it would be a sure thing: 貸してくれます, "he'll lend it".

Said with a rising voice, でしょう？ turns into "right?": you're pretty sure and want the other person to agree.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 7

旅行りょこう演習えんしゅうしたいって言いったのペンギンさんでしょ。

"You're the one who said you wanted to practice traveling, Penguin, right?"

Casual version: the short でしょ. Men and women both use it with friends, mostly for "right?". Here he's reminding Penguin whose idea this was.

Examples

A client asks when the sketches will be done.

金曜きんよう日ひには終おわるでしょう。

"They'll probably be done by Friday."

Polite

Someone at the shop asks if the cake is still fresh.

今日きょう中じゅうなら大丈夫だいじょうぶでしょう。

"It should be fine if you eat it today."

大丈夫 + でしょう, no だ in between.

Polite

Your friend lies on the couch after a long walk.

疲つかれたでしょ？

"You're tired, right?"

Casual

Your friend can't find their keys.

カバンの中なかでしょ？

"They're in your bag, right?"

Casual

With and without

Without

明日あしたは雨あめです。

"It's going to rain tomorrow." Sure, like you already know.

With でしょう

明日あしたは雨あめでしょう。

"It'll probably rain tomorrow." A guess. What the weather forecast says.

Without

疲つかれた。

"I'm tired." About you.

With でしょ？

疲つかれたでしょ？

"You're tired, right?" About them, asking them to agree.

Sentence mining

Polite

New Atashin'chi · Episode 1

冷蔵れいぞう庫こに…煮豆にまめがあったでしょう？

"There were simmered beans in the fridge, right?"

Rising でしょう？: "right?". Even at home people use the full でしょう for this.

Polite

YouTube · video

しかし本当ほんとうにそうなのでしょうか。

"But is that really true?"

Same でしょうか, used to make you doubt it.

Polite

Legal High · Episode 5

でしょう。

"Isn't it?"

でしょう on its own: "isn't it?", "I told you so". She's sure you agree.

Casual

New Atashin'chi · Episode 1

裁縫さいほうセット持もってるでしょ..貸かして

"You have a sewing kit, right? Lend it to me."

でしょ checks first ("you have one, right?"), then she asks for it.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 10

餃子ぎょうざ…　メニューにないでしょ

"Gyoza... that's not on the menu, right?"

でしょ = "right?" when you're pretty sure. Short spoken form of でしょう.

Casual

Overprotected Kahoko · Episode 5

ウソでしょ？

"No way."

ウソ ("a lie") + でしょ = "that's a lie, right?", meaning "no way, you're kidding".

Casual

Good Morning Call · Episode 1

でしょ？

"Right?"

でしょ on its own: "right?", asking the other person to agree.

Tae Kim's Guide to Japanese Grammar

Various degrees of certainty · Using 「でしょう」 (polite)

Various degrees of certainty · 「でしょう」 and 「だろう」 (casual)

N5 Grammar

だろう

Casual

He Who Can't Marry · Episode 1

俺おれの受うけ売うりだろう？

"That's [just] what I told you, right?"

だろう does the same job as でしょう: "probably", or with a rising voice "right?". It goes at the very end, after a plain verb, an い-adjective, or a noun (no だ before it).

On this card, he's pretty sure where the other guy got that idea, so it's "right?". Said out loud to someone, だろう and the short だろ sound masculine and a bit blunt. Most women, and plenty of men, say でしょ instead.

Two places where だろう is neutral and everyone uses it: "I wonder..." (なんだろう, said to yourself), and writing or inner thoughts.

Examples

You look at the dark clouds and say it to yourself.

明日あしたも雨あめだろうな。

"It'll probably rain tomorrow too."

Talking to yourself, so it's fine for anyone. な makes it a thought.

Casual

Two guys after football practice.

疲つかれただろ？

"You're tired, right?"

Masculine. A woman would say 疲れたでしょ？

Casual

You find a strange box on your doorstep.

これ、なんだろう？

"I wonder what this is."

Question word + だろう: "I wonder". Used by everyone.

Casual

Your friend is late and not answering.

どこにいるんだろう。

"I wonder where they are."

Casual

With and without

だろ？

疲つかれただろ？

"You're tired, right?" Masculine, a bit rough.

でしょ？

疲つかれたでしょ？

Same meaning. Neutral, anyone can say it.

Without

これ、なに？

"What's this?" Asking someone.

With だろう

これ、なんだろう？

"I wonder what this is." Asking yourself, nobody needs to answer.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 5

どうやったら彼女かのじょのハートを射止いとめることができるんだろう。

"I wonder how I can win her heart."

Question word (どうやったら) + んだろう: "I wonder...", said to himself.

Casual

YouTube · video

どうやって撃退げきたいすればいいんだろう?

"How am I supposed to fight them off?"

Same "I wonder" だろう, thinking out loud while playing.

Casual

YouTube · video

で、とりあえず基地きちを作つくりなさいよっていうようなことなんだろうな。

"So I guess for now it's telling me to build a base."

"Probably" だろう + な: guessing to himself what the game wants.

Casual

Sailor Suit and Machine Gun · Episode 3

だろうな…

"I figured."

だろう + な on its own: "I figured", "I thought so". Said to himself.

Casual

The Cat Returns

当然とうぜんだろ。

"Of course."

当然 ("of course, natural") + だろ = "obviously, right?". Rough and masculine.

Casual

The Girl Who Leapt Through Time

"What's that?"

何 ("what") + だろう = "I wonder what it is". Question word + だろう is for everyone.

Casual

My Neighbor Totoro

"Who could that be?"

誰 ("who") + だろう = "I wonder who it is".

な、うまいだろ。

"See, it's good, right?"

だろ, the short form, expecting you to agree.

A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

Entry "darō" · pp. 100–102

Tae Kim's Guide to Japanese Grammar

Various degrees of certainty · 「でしょう」 and 「だろう」 (casual)

N5 Grammar

い-Adjective

Polite～いです
Casual～い

Same meaning. Only the politeness changes. The adjective itself stays the same.

Casual

YouTube · video

いつもよりおいしい。

"[It's] tastier than usual."

An い-adjective describes something and ends in い: おいしい (tasty), 寒い (cold), 高い (expensive). It can end a sentence just as it is, no だ needed.

On this card, someone tastes it and compares it to normal. いつもより is "than usual". The sentence answers "How is it?".

Polite: add です, おいしいです. Before a noun it goes straight on, no な: おいしいラーメン.

Polite

YouTube · video

セブンの春巻はるまきが1番ばん美味おいしいです。

"The spring rolls at Seven [Eleven] are the tastiest."

です goes right after the adjective. 1番 is "the most".

Examples

You step outside in August.

暑あつい！

"It's hot!"

One word is a full sentence. No だ after an い-adjective.

Casual

A shop clerk shows you a bag. You check the price tag.

ちょっと高たかいですね。

"It's a bit expensive."

Polite

A friend notices your shoes.

新あたらしい靴くつ？

"New shoes?"

新しい goes right before 靴. No な in between.

Casual

Your boss asks what your new teacher is like.

優やさしい先生せんせいです。

"She's a kind teacher."

優しい describes 先生. The です at the end is for the whole sentence.

Polite

With and without

Just the noun

日ひ

"A day." Could be any day.

Before a noun

寒さむい日ひ

"A cold day." The adjective goes straight in front.

End of sentence

今日きょうは寒さむいです。

"It's cold today." Drop です for casual: 今日は寒い。

Not this

寒さむいな日ひ

な is only for な-adjectives (静かな日). An い-adjective never takes it.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

たい焼やきは、魚さかなの形かたちをした甘あまいおやつです。

"Taiyaki is a sweet, fish-shaped snack."

甘い (sweet) goes right before おやつ (snack). 魚の形をした (fish-shaped) describes the snack too.

Polite

Border · Episode 9

痛いたいですよ

"That hurts."

痛い ("painful") + です: polite.

Polite

Million Yen Woman · Episode 5

共同きょうどう生活せいかつ　なかなか楽たのしいですよ

"Living together is actually pretty fun."

楽しい ("fun") + です. なかなか means "quite, more than you'd think".

Casual

YouTube · video

ちょっと奥行おくゆきが狭せまい。

"It's a bit shallow."

奥行き is how deep something is, 狭い is "narrow, tight". The adjective ends the sentence as it is.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 4

寝ねっ転ころがるには狭せまいしさ

"It's too small to lie down in."

狭い straight at the end, no です. Casual.

Casual

YouTube · video

あ、ライフル弾だん嬉うれしい。

"Oh, rifle ammo, nice."

嬉しい (glad, happy) ends the sentence on its own. Literally "rifle ammo, I'm glad".

Casual

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 1

すごい おいしい。

"It's really delicious."

すごい ("amazing") + おいしい ("delicious"). In speech, すごい often works like "really": "really delicious".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 44

かわいいね。

"It's cute, isn't it."

い-adjectives can end a sentence, no だ.

Reference

A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

Tae Kim's Guide to Japanese Grammar

Adjectives · The i-adjective

N5 Grammar

いい (良い)

Politeいいです
Casualいい

Same meaning: "it's good". Only the politeness changes.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 5

ふーん和わのテイストもいいけど

"Hmm, a Japanese style is nice too, but..."

いい means "good" or "nice". It's an い-adjective: put it at the end to say something is good, or right before a noun: いい天気 (good weather).

On this card, he's weighing ideas and likes the Japanese-style one. 和 is "Japanese", テイスト is "taste, style". It answers "Is it good?".

Polite: いいです. Watch out: every other form comes from 良い (よい): よくない (not good), よかった (was good). Never いくない or いかった.

Polite

YouTube · video

やっぱり息いきが切きれるけどいい運動うんどうですね

"I still get out of breath, but it's good exercise."

Here いい sits right before a noun: いい運動, good exercise. The です at the end makes it polite.

Examples

You open the curtains. Blue sky.

いい天気てんき！

"Nice weather!"

いい right before a noun, like any い-adjective. No な needed.

Casual

A friend asks if they can borrow your pen.

いいよ。

"Sure."

Here いい is "okay, fine", not "good".

Casual

A colleague asks how the new office chairs are.

すごくいいです。

"They're really good."

Polite

A friend asks how your knee is after the run.

あんまりよくない。

"Not great."

"Not good" is よくない, never いくない. It comes from 良い.

Casual

With and without

Good

天気てんきがいい。

"The weather's good." Right now, plain and simple.

Not good

天気てんきがよくない。

"The weather's not good." Switches to よ.

Was good

天気てんきがよかった。

"The weather was good." Also よ.

Not this

いくない・いかった

Feels logical, sounds wrong. Only the plain "good" uses いい.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

箱根はこねにもいい温泉おんせんがたくさんありますね。

"Hakone has lots of nice hot springs too."

いい right before the noun: いい温泉, good hot springs.

Polite

YouTube · video

赤あかちゃん、ベビーカーでもいいと思おもいます。

"I think it's fine with a baby or a stroller too."

でもいい is "is fine too". Again いい as "okay".

Polite

Million Yen Woman · Episode 9

いいですね。

"Sounds good."

いい ("good") + ですね = "that's nice", "sounds good". Agreeing with an idea.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 4

ああいうのもかっこいいな

"Something like that is cool too."

かっこいい means "cool". な at the end: thinking out loud.

Casual

YouTube · video

ま、両親りょうしんとすごく仲なかがいいとか

"Well, like, I get along really well with my parents."

仲がいい is "the relationship is good", so "get along well".

Casual

YouTube · Japanese Listening Practice With A Story (Informal) #3

みどりさん準備じゅんびはいい

"Midori, are you ready?"

準備 is "preparation", so this is literally "Is your prep good?", which is just "Ready?". いい as "okay".

Casual

YouTube · Japanese Demonstrative Pronoun #1

はははいいよ気きにしないで

"Hahaha, it's okay, don't worry about it."

いいよ here is "it's fine", not "good".

Reference

A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

Appendix 1, Basic Conjugations · pp. 580–581

Tae Kim's Guide to Japanese Grammar

Adjectives · An annoying exception

N5 Grammar

な-Adjective

Polite～です
Casual～だ plain statement
～ nothing added, very common

Same meaning: "it's ...". Before a noun it's always な: ～な + noun.

Polite

YouTube · video

ここが上高地かみこうちで一番いちばん有名ゆうめいな場所ばしょです。

"This is the most famous spot in Kamikochi."

A な-adjective is a describing word like 有名 (famous), 静か (quiet), きれい (pretty). When it sits right before a noun, you add な in between: 有名 + な + 場所.

On this card, a vlogger walks up to the river and the bridge. The adjective answers "What kind of place is this?": the most famous one. 一番 is "the most".

The な only shows up before a noun. At the end of a sentence it's gone (see the next card).

Polite

YouTube · video

ここ、夜景やけいがきれいです。

"The night view here is pretty."

Here きれい ends the sentence, so no な: just きれいです. Before a noun it would be きれいな夜景. Casual: きれいだ, or just きれい. Careful: きれい ends in い, but it's a な-adjective.

Casual

Good Morning Call · Season 2, Episode 2

あのキレイな人ひとは？

"Who's that pretty woman?"

な connects a な-adjective to the noun after it. On this card, キレイ + な + 人, and キレイ is the same word as きれい, in katakana for style.

Examples

A friend asks what your studio in Chigasaki is like.

静しずかな部屋へやです。

"It's a quiet room."

静か comes before 部屋, so な goes in between.

Polite

The same friend stays over and notices how quiet it is at night.

静しずかだね。

"It's quiet, huh."

Same word, end of the sentence, so no な. だ is the casual です.

Casual

Someone asks about your favorite food.

好すきな食たべ物ものはカレー。

"My favorite food is curry."

好き looks like a verb in English ("to like"), but it's a な-adjective: 好き + な + 食べ物.

Casual

You trip on the stairs. A coworker rushes over.

大丈夫だいじょうぶです。

"I'm okay."

Nothing comes after 大丈夫 but です, so no な.

Polite

With and without

Before a noun

静しずかな町まち

"A quiet town." な connects the adjective to the noun.

End of sentence

この町まちは静しずかです。

"This town is quiet." No な. Casual: 静かだ, or just 静か.

い-adjective

寒さむい日ひ

"A cold day." い-adjectives go straight before the noun, no な.

Not this

静しずか町まち · 静しずかなです

No な before a noun, or な at the end. Both are wrong.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

味噌みそ汁しるは、日本にほん食しょくに欠かかせない大切たいせつな料理りょうりです。

"Miso soup is an important dish, you can't have Japanese food without it."

大切 (important) + な + 料理 (dish).

Polite

Border · Episode 7

有名ゆうめいな政治せいじ家かの息子むすこです

"He's the son of a famous politician."

有名 + な + 政治家 ("politician").

Casual

YouTube · video

急きゅうな坂道さかみちを登のぼる。

"Climbing a steep slope."

急 (steep) + な + 坂道 (slope).

Casual

YouTube · video

な、ちょっとなんか厚あつみがないからなんか変へんな感かんじするな。

"Hmm, it's kind of thin, so it feels a bit weird."

変 (strange) + な + 感じ (feeling). The な at the very start and end is a different one: a "huh" said to yourself.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 4

後部こうぶ座席ざせきって微妙びみょうだよね

"The back seat is kind of meh, right?"

微妙 (so-so, iffy) ends the sentence, so no な, just だ (the casual です). って works like は here.

Casual

Weakest Beast · Episode 10

あら～ きれいな花はな　どうも

"Oh, what pretty flowers. Thank you."

きれい + な + 花: な joins it to the noun.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 45

今日きょうは暇ひまだね。

"It's quiet today."

暇 is a な-adjective, here with だ at the end.

Reference

A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

Appendix 1, Basic Conjugations · pp. 580–581

Tae Kim's Guide to Japanese Grammar

Adjectives · The na-adjective

N5 Grammar

い-Adjective (Negative)

Polite～くないです everyday, softer
～くありません standard polite, a bit firmer
Casual～くない drop the い, add くない

Same meaning: "isn't". Only the politeness changes.

高い → 高くない

おもしろい → おもしろくない

The last い goes, く takes its place, then add ない.

The one exceptionいい → よくない never いくない

Why: いい comes from an older word for "good", よい. The negative still uses よい: よい → よくない.

More on the いい page.

Casual

YouTube · video

じゃあ、あんまり名古屋なごや詳くわしくない。

"Well, [then] I don't really know Nagoya that well."

To say something is not a certain way, swap the last い of an い-adjective for くない: 詳しい (knows well) → 詳しくない (doesn't know well).

On this card, the speaker just worked out they've barely spent time in Nagoya. あんまり + くない is "not very". It answers "Do you know Nagoya?".

Watch out: いい becomes よくない, never いくない.

Polite

Quartet · Episode 3

全然ぜんぜん面白おもしろくないです

"It's not funny at all."

Add です to the casual form to make it polite. On this card, 面白い → 面白くない → 面白くないです, and 全然 means "at all".

Examples

A friend worries the hike will be too much for you.

大丈夫だいじょうぶ、そんなに遠とおくないよ。

"It's fine, it's not that far."

Casual

The shop clerk asks if the coat is too heavy.

いえ、全然ぜんぜん重おもくないです。

"No, it's not heavy at all."

For polite, just put です after くない.

Polite

Someone offers you the spicy curry. You try it.

あれ、辛からくない。

"Huh, it's not spicy."

Casual

A coworker asks how you're feeling today.

ちょっと調子ちょうしがよくないです。

"I'm not feeling great."

いい is the odd one. It turns into よくない, never いくない.

Polite

With and without

Is

高たかい。

"It's expensive."

Isn't

高たかくない。

"It's not expensive." Drop the い, add くない.

Polite

高たかくないです。

Same thing, polite. Also fine: 高くありません, a bit stiffer.

Not this

高たかいじゃない。

じゃない is for nouns and な-adjectives. い-adjectives use くない.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

汚きたなくないけど、昨日きのう、昨日きのうと昨日きのうにたくさん雨あめが降ふったからちょっと濁にごっていますね。

"It's not dirty, but it rained a lot the last couple of days, so it's a bit murky."

汚い (dirty) → 汚くない. Then けど, "but".

Polite

Source unknown No source

ヤンキーとか、全然ぜんぜん怖こわくないっすね。

"I'm not scared of yankii at all."

っす is a slangy です. 全然 + くない is "not at all".

Polite

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 7

全然ぜんぜん よくないんですけど。

"It's not okay at all."

Exception: いい → よくない. 全然 ("at all") + よくない ("not good") = "not okay at all". んですけど adds "just so you know".

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 36

よくありません！

"It's not okay!"

Exception: いい → よくない. Polite: よくありません.

Casual

Source unknown No source

なんか、この雪山ゆきやまを渡わたってるから、余計よけいに良よくない気きがする。

"Somehow it feels even worse because we're crossing this snowy mountain."

Exception: いい → よくない. 良くない is the same word, written in kanji. 良くない気がする: "feels like it's not good".

Casual

Border · Episode 6

顔色かおいろ 良よくないぞ。

"You don't look well."

Exception: いい → よくない. 良くない is the same word, written in kanji. 顔色 ("complexion") + 良くない = "you look pale". ぞ: rough "I'm telling you".

Casual

Only Yesterday

あんまり甘あまくないのね…

"It's not that sweet, huh."

甘い ("sweet"): drop い, add くない = 甘くない, "not sweet". あんまり: "not that".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 41

痛いたくないから。

"Because it doesn't hurt."

痛い drops い, adds くない.

Adjectives · The i-adjective

Polite Form and Verb Stems · Using 「です」 for everything else

N5 Grammar

い-Adjective (Past)

Polite～かったです
Casual～かった drop the い, add かった

Same meaning: "was". Only the politeness changes.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 14

楽たのしかったね。

"[Today at the beach] was fun, huh."

To say how something was, swap the last い of an い-adjective for かった: 楽しい (fun) → 楽しかった (was fun).

On this card, friends look back on a day at the sea that's just over. The ね at the end is "huh", checking the other person feels the same. It answers "How was it?".

Polite: 楽しかったです. Never 楽しいでした: the past is already in かった. Watch out: いい becomes 良かった, never いかった.

Polite

Midnight Diner

こないだ教おしえていただいた寿司すし屋やホントうまかったです。

"That sushi place you told me about the other day was really good."

Just add です after かった: うまい (tasty) → うまかった → うまかったです. On this card, someone is thanking the person who recommended a sushi place.

Examples

A friend asks how your trip to Hokkaido was.

寒さむかった！

"It was cold!"

Casual

You leave a ramen place, still full.

おいしかったね。

"That was good, huh."

Casual

A colleague asks about the movie you saw at the weekend.

面白おもしろかったです。

"It was interesting."

For polite, just put です after かった. Not 面白いでした.

Polite

A friend asks how the concert was.

よかったよ。

"It was good."

いい is the odd one. It turns into よかった, never いかった.

Casual

With and without

Now

寒さむい。

"It's cold." You're standing in it right now.

Was

寒さむかった。

"It was cold." You're home now, telling the story.

Polite

寒さむかったです。

かった does the past, です just adds politeness.

Not this

寒さむいでした。

Feels logical, sounds wrong. です never carries the past here.

Sentence mining

Polite

Source unknown No source

めっちゃ気持きもちよかったです。

"It felt really good."

いい turns into よかった, so 気持ちいい (feels good) becomes 気持ちよかった. Then です for politeness.

Polite

Kekkon Dekinai Otoko · Episode 2

いや いや いや 危あぶなかったですね

"Whoa, whoa, that was a close one."

危ない (dangerous) drops い and adds かった, then です for politeness.

Polite

Demon Slayer · Season 1, Episode 8

おいしかったです

"That was delicious."

Said right after finishing a meal. おいしい drops い and adds かった, and です makes it polite.

Casual

Good Morning Call · Episode 16

忙いそがしかった？

"Were you busy?"

忙しい becomes 忙しかった. For a casual question, just raise your voice at the end.

Casual

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 7

すごいうれしかった。

"I was so happy."

うれしい becomes うれしかった. She is remembering a moment that's over.

Casual

Kotaro Lives Alone · Episode 4

それはもうひどかった

"It was just awful."

ひどい (awful) becomes ひどかった. This is someone's first impression of a person, looking back.

Casual

Japan Sinks: 2020 · Season 1, Episode 1

俺おれ　ちょっと怖こわかったけどなあ

"I was kinda scared, though."

怖い becomes 怖かった. He's looking back at a moment that's over. The けどなあ at the end is just "though..." trailing off.

Casual

Source unknown No source

それなら良よかった！

"Oh, in that case, I'm glad!"

Literally "it was good", and it's how Japanese says "I'm glad". いい becomes 良かった, never いかった.

A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

Tae Kim's Guide to Japanese Grammar

Adjectives · The i-adjective

Polite Form and Verb Stems · Using 「です」 for everything else

N5 Grammar

い-Adjective (Past negative)

Polite～くなかったです everyday, softer
～くありませんでした standard polite, a bit firmer
Casual～くなかった drop the い, add くなかった

Same meaning: "wasn't". Only the politeness changes.

Polite

Million Yen Woman · Episode 7

全まったく面白おもしろくなかったです

"It wasn't interesting at all."

To say an い-adjective wasn't something in the past, drop the い and add くなかった. Add です to make it polite.

On this card, 面白い → 面白くなかった → 面白くなかったです, and 全く means "at all".

Casual

Good Morning Call · Episode 1

でも 本当ほんとうは 面白おもしろくなかっただろ

"But it really wasn't fun, right?"

The same form with no です is casual. On this card, だろ at the end adds "right?".

Examples

A friend asks about the horror movie you saw last night.

全然ぜんぜん怖こわくなかった。

"It wasn't scary at all."

Casual

Your boss asks if the test was hard.

そんなに難むずかしくなかったです。

"It wasn't that hard."

For polite, just put です after くなかった.

Polite

You tried the new ramen place. Meh.

あまりおいしくなかったな。

"It wasn't that good."

Casual

A friend asks how the weather was on your trip.

天気てんきはよくなかった。

"The weather wasn't good."

いい is the odd one. It turns into よくなかった, never いくなかった.

Casual

With and without

Was

寒さむかった。

"It was cold."

Wasn't

寒さむくなかった。

"It wasn't cold." Drop the い, add くなかった.

Polite

寒さむくなかったです。

Same thing, polite. Also fine: 寒くありませんでした, a bit stiffer.

Not this

寒さむいじゃなかった。

じゃなかった is for nouns and な-adjectives. い-adjectives use くなかった.

Sentence mining

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 18

あれ？怖こわくなかったですか？

"Huh? Wasn't it scary?"

くなかった + です is the polite version.

Polite

Clannad · Episode 1

お、おいしくありませんでしたか？

"W-was it not good?"

おいしい drops い, adds くありませんでした. The stiffer polite form, same meaning as おいしくなかったですか.

Casual

Fairy Tail · Episode 56

相手あいてが よくなかった。

"You were up against the wrong opponent."

Literally "the opponent wasn't good", meaning not a good match-up for you, not that they were weak. いい → よくなかった.

Casual

I am Mita, Your Housekeeper · Episode 2

痛いたくなかった？

"Didn't it hurt?"

痛い ("painful") → 痛くない → 痛くなかった = "didn't hurt". Rising voice: "didn't it hurt?".

Casual

Million Yen Woman · Episode 1

おいしくなかった？

"Was it not good?"

おいしい ("tasty") → おいしくなかった = "wasn't tasty". Rising voice makes it a question.

Casual

Frieren Beyond Journey's End · Episode 4

もしかして あまり楽たのしくなかった？

"Could it be you didn't enjoy it much?"

あまり ("not very") + 楽しくなかった ("wasn't fun") = "wasn't much fun". もしかして: "could it be...".

Casual

Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood · Episode 23

貴様きさまのトラップ、悪わるくなかった。

"Your trap wasn't bad."

悪い ("bad") → 悪くなかった = "wasn't bad", a grudging bit of praise. 貴様: a very rough "you".

Casual

From the New World · Episode 10

あの猫ねこだって 別べつに悪わるくなかったんだ。

"Even that cat did nothing wrong."

悪い ("bad") → 悪くなかった = "did nothing wrong". あの猫だって: "even that cat".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 24

そんなすごくなかったでしょ。

"It wasn't that great, was it."

すごい drops い, adds くなかった.

Reference

A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

Appendix 1, Basic Conjugations · pp. 580–581

Tae Kim's Guide to Japanese Grammar

Adjectives · The i-adjective

Polite Form and Verb Stems · Using 「です」 for everything else

N5 Grammar

な-Adjective (Negative)

Polite～じゃないです everyday, softer
～じゃありません standard polite, a bit firmer
～ではありません most formal: news, speeches, writing
Casual～じゃない no な before it

Same meaning: "isn't". Only the politeness changes.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 4

ちっとも便利べんりじゃないわねスマホ

"Smartphones aren't handy at all, are they?"

To say a な-adjective is not, add じゃない right after it, no な: 便利 (handy) → 便利じゃない. It works exactly like a noun: 学生じゃない.

On this card, the speaker is fed up with her phone. The sentence answers "Are smartphones handy?": not one bit. ちっとも is "not at all", and わね is a soft "aren't they".

Watch out: 綺麗 and 嫌い end in い but are な-adjectives, so 綺麗じゃない, never 綺麗くない.

Polite

Fairy Tail · Episode 133

大丈夫だいじょうぶですか？ 大丈夫だいじょうぶじゃありません…

"Are you okay? No, I'm not okay..."

じゃありません is a polite "isn't", with no な before it. On this card, the question uses 大丈夫です and the answer turns it into 大丈夫じゃありません.

Examples

A friend picks up the new game you've been playing and asks if it's easy.

簡単かんたんじゃないよ。

"It's not easy."

簡単 (easy) + じゃない.

Casual

A coworker asks if you can help out tonight.

すみません、今日きょうは暇ひまじゃないです。

"Sorry, I'm not free today."

Polite

A friend offers you natto.

ごめん、納豆なっとうは好すきじゃない。

"Sorry, I don't like natto."

好き is a な-adjective too, so 好きじゃない.

Casual

The hotel staff asks how your room is.

あまり静しずかじゃありません。

"It's not very quiet."

じゃありません is the stiffer polite one. Same meaning as じゃないです.

Polite

With and without

Is

静しずかだ。

"It's quiet."

Isn't

静しずかじゃない。

"It's not quiet." Just add じゃない.

Polite

静しずかじゃないです。

Same thing, polite. Also fine: 静かじゃありません.

Not this

静しずかくない。

くない is for い-adjectives (高い → 高くない). な-adjectives use じゃない.

N5 Grammar

な-Adjective (Past)

Polite～でした
Casual～だった

Same meaning: "was". Only the politeness changes.

Polite

YouTube · video

想像そうぞう以上いじょうに綺麗きれいでした。

"It was even more beautiful than I imagined."

To say how something was with a な-adjective, add だった right after it, no な: 綺麗 → 綺麗だった. It works exactly like a noun: 学生だった.

On this card, the speaker just saw the place. The sentence answers "How was it?": beautiful, more than expected. 想像以上に is "beyond what I imagined".

Polite: でした, like on this card: 綺麗でした. Watch out: 綺麗 ends in い but is a な-adjective, so never 綺麗かった.

Casual

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 5

久ひさしぶり 元気げんきだった？

"Long time no see. How have you been?"

だった is the casual でした. On this card, 元気 + だった = "were you well?", and the rising voice makes it a question.

Examples

A friend asks how the new hotel was.

すごく静しずかだったよ。

"It was really quiet."

Casual

A coworker asks about your move.

大変たいへんでした。

"It was tough."

Polite

Your friend asks if you still play the piano.

子こどもの頃ころは好すきだったけど…。

"I liked it as a kid, but…"

好き is a な-adjective too, so 好きだった.

Casual

Someone asks how the hotel location was.

駅えきの前まえで、便利べんりでした。

"It was right by the station, so it was handy."

Polite

With and without

Now

元気げんきだ。

"I'm fine." Right now.

Was

元気げんきだった。

"I was fine." Just add だった.

Polite

元気げんきでした。

Same thing, polite.

Not this

綺麗きれいかった。

かった is for い-adjectives (高い → 高かった). 綺麗 only looks like one.

必要 (needed) is a な-adjective: 必要でした, "was needed".

N5 Grammar

好き・嫌い

Casual

Terrace House

馬刺ばさしが好すき。

"I like horse sashimi."

好き means "liked". It's not a verb, it's a な-adjective that describes the thing: "horse sashimi is liked (by me)". So the thing you like gets が, not を.

On this card, the answer to "What do you like?" is 馬刺し (horse sashimi) + が + 好き.

好き or 好きだ is casual, 好きです is polite. Before a noun it takes な: 好きな食べ物, "favorite food".

Polite

YouTube · video

じゃあ、名古屋なごやの嫌きらいなところは何なんですか?

"So what do you dislike about Nagoya?"

嫌い is the opposite, "disliked", and works exactly like 好き: が before it, な before a noun (嫌いなところ). It ends in い but it's a な-adjective, so never 嫌くない.

嫌い is strong, close to "hate". To say "I don't really like it", people usually say あまり好きじゃない.

Examples

A new coworker asks what you do on weekends.

山やまが好すきです。よく登のぼります。

"I like mountains. I climb a lot."

The thing you like + が + 好きです.

Polite

A friend offers you natto at breakfast.

ごめん、納豆なっとう嫌きらい。

"Sorry, I hate natto."

Casual: plain 嫌い, and the が drops out.

Casual

Your host asks if you eat spicy food.

辛つらいものはあまり好すきじゃないです。

"I don't really like spicy food."

The soft way to say you dislike something. は instead of が, because you're contrasting it with other food.

Polite

Two friends scrolling through a music app.

好すきなバンドある？

"Got a favorite band?"

好き + な + noun: "a band you like", which is how Japanese says "favorite".

Casual

With and without

Without

猫ねこです。

"It's a cat." You're just naming it.

With 好き

猫ねこが好すきです。

"I like cats." Now it's about how you feel about it.

Without

食たべ物ものは何なんですか？

"What's the food?" Just asking which food it is.

With 嫌いな

嫌きらいな食たべ物ものは何なんですか？

"What food do you dislike?" 嫌い + な describes the food.

Add か to ask "do you like...?". は instead of が because fast food is the topic she's bringing up.

Question word + が + 好きですか: "which ... do you like?"

好き ("like") + ですよ = "I do like it". よ: telling them plainly, in case they doubted it.

好き + です, polite.

サウナ ("sauna") + が + 好き + なんだ = "I like saunas, you see". なんだ explains something about himself.

The soft "dislike": あまり好きじゃない instead of 嫌い.

これ + が + 好き: が marks what you like.

N5 Grammar

～のが好き

To say you like doing something, put のが after the verb, then 好き: 泳ぐのが好き, "I like swimming". The の turns the action into a thing you can like.

The verb stays in its dictionary form (泳ぐ, 見る, 作る). The same frame works with 大好き, 嫌い, 得意 ("good at") and 苦手 ("bad at, not into"). Polite or casual only shows at the end: 好きです / 好きだ / just 好き.

Examples

Introducing yourself at a new job.

料理りょうりを作つくるのが好すきです。

"I like cooking."

Polite

A coworker asks if you're a morning person.

朝あさ早はやく起おきるのが嫌きらいです。

"I hate getting up early."

Same frame with 嫌い: 起きる + のが嫌い.

Polite

A friend asks why you went to the cinema alone.

一人ひとりで映画えいがを見みるのが好すきなんだ。

"I just like watching movies on my own."

Casual

Your friend notices the camera you always carry.

写真しゃしんを撮とるのが大好だいすき！

"I love taking photos!"

Casual

With and without

Without

音楽おんがくが好すきです。

"I like music." You like a thing.

With のが好き

音楽おんがくを聞きくのが好すきです。

"I like listening to music." You like doing something.

Noun-related Particles · The 「の」 particle

N5 Grammar

上手・下手

Examples

Your friend sings at karaoke and nails it.

歌うたが上手じょうずだね！

"You're good at singing!"

The thing someone is good at + が + 上手. Same as 好き: が, not を.

Casual

A coworker asks if you cook at home.

いえ、料理りょうりが下手へたなんです。

"No, I'm bad at cooking."

下手 about yourself is fine. It sounds modest.

Polite

You watch a kid at the pool.

泳およぐのが上手じょうずですね。

"He's good at swimming."

With a verb, add の first: 泳ぐ + の + が. The の turns the action into a noun, because が can't come right after a verb. 泳ぐが上手 is wrong.

Polite

Your friend can't fix their bike.

もっと上手じょうずな人ひとに聞きいて。

"Ask someone who's better at it."

上手 and 下手 are な-adjectives, so before a noun they take な: 上手な人, a skilled person.

Casual

At a job interview: "What are you good at?"

料理りょうりが得意とくいです。

"Cooking is my strong point."

Don't say 上手 about yourself, it sounds like bragging. Say 得意 (my strong point) instead. The opposite is 苦手 (my weak point, "not my thing"). Both work like 上手: が before, な before a noun.

Polite

With and without

Without

歌うたが好すきだね。

"You like singing." Says nothing about how well.

With 上手

歌うたが上手じょうずだね。

"You're good at singing." Now it's about skill.

Without

毎日まいにち泳およぎます。

"I swim every day." Just what you do.

With のが下手

泳およぐのが下手へたです。

"I'm bad at swimming." Verb + の + が + 下手.

Polite

全ぜん日本にほんの女子じょしバレーボールチームは、上手じょうずです。

"Japan's women's volleyball team is good."

No が here: what they're good at is obvious, so just 上手です.

Polite

祖父そふは、木工もっこう品ひんを作つくるのが得意とくいです。

"My grandpa is great at making things out of wood."

得意 works like 上手: verb + の + が + 得意.

Polite

Fairy Tail · Episode 152

はい、とっても上手じょうずです。

"Yes, you're really good!"

上手です: you're good at it. Said about someone else, never yourself.

Casual

Source unknown No source

考かんがえてはいるけど伝つたえられない？そう、何なにか話はなすの下手へたなの。

"You think it, but can't say it? Yeah, I'm just bad at talking."

Verb + の + 下手. In casual speech the が often drops out.

Casual

下手へたなマッサージより、スパにいきたいよ。

"I'd rather go to a spa than get a bad massage."

下手 + な + noun: a massage done badly.

三田みた 料理りょうりとっても上手じょうずなんだよ。

Skill + 上手: 料理(が)上手, good at cooking.

Casual

ごめんね、下手へたな演奏えんそうで。

"Sorry it was so bad."

下手 is a な-adjective, so before a noun it takes な: 下手な演奏, a clumsy performance.

Casual

それに、結構けっこう料理りょうりも上手じょうずだし…

N5 Grammar

～くなる・～になる

Polite

YouTube · video

でも、大人おとなになって、温泉おんせんが好すきになりました。

"But once I grew up, I came to like hot springs." [as a kid I didn't]

なる means to become: something changes from one state to another. After a noun or a な-adjective, add に: 大人になる = "become an adult", 好きになる = "come to like".

On this card, it answers "what changed?": before, he wasn't an adult and didn't like onsen. Now both are true.

Polite: なります / なりました. Casual: なる / なった.

Polite

YouTube · video

え、お家いえをちょっと、え、改築かいちくして大おおきくなりました。

"Um, we remodeled the house a bit, and it got bigger."

With an い-adjective, swap the last い for く: 大きい → 大きくなる = "get bigger". No に here.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 40

寒さむくなったね。

"It's gotten cold."

An い-adjective drops い and adds く + なる. On this card, 寒い ("cold") → 寒くなった = "has gotten cold".

Examples

You see Mt. Fuji on a cold morning, the day after it snowed.

富士ふじ山やまが雪ゆきで白しろくなった。

"Mt. Fuji turned white with snow."

白い ("white") → 白く + なった ("became") = "turned white". The い turns into く before なる. Don't mix it up with 白くなかった ("wasn't white").

Casual

A kid asks what you wanted to be when you were little.

医者いしゃになりたかったです。

"I wanted to become a doctor."

医者 is a noun, so it's 医者になる.

Polite

Your friend's Japanese has improved a lot.

日本にほん語ご、上手じょうずになったね！

"Your Japanese got really good!"

上手 is a な-adjective, so it takes に too: 上手になる.

Casual

You look at the clock while gaming.

え、もう十じゅう時じになった！

"Wait, it's already ten?!"

Times "become" too: it turned ten o'clock.

Casual

You look at the price tag again after a year.

高たかくなりましたね。

"It's gotten more expensive."

高い → 高く. The い always turns into く before なる.

Polite

With and without

Without

部屋へやが暗くらい。

"The room is dark." Just how it is right now.

With なる

部屋へやが暗くらくなった。

"The room got dark." It was bright before, and something changed: the sun went down, the light went off.

Polite

とても緊張きんちょうして、頭あたまが真まっ白しろになりました。

"I was so nervous my mind went blank."

Literally "my head became pure white". 真っ白 is a な-adjective, so に.

Polite

これは迷子まいごになりますよ。

"You could totally get lost here."

迷子 means "lost child", so 迷子になる is "become lost". The everyday way to say "get lost".

"None of our friends will come anymore."

ない → なくなる: it gets to the point where nobody comes.

Polite

遅おそくなりましたけど、持もってきました。

"Sorry it's late, but I brought it."

遅い → 遅くなる: became late.

Casual

すれ違ちがいになったら大変たいへん。

"It'd be a pain if we ended up missing each other."

すれ違い (missing each other) is a noun, so に. なったら = "if it becomes".

Casual

ケンカになって

"...and it turned into a fight."

ケンカ ("a fight") + に + なって ("became, and...") = "it turned into a fight". Nouns take に before なる.

Casual

"Why don't you just be honest?"

素直 ("honest, open") + に + なったら ("if you became") = "why don't you just be honest?".

N5 Grammar

～すぎる

Polite～すぎます
Casual～すぎる・～すぎ すぎ alone: spoken, very casual

Same meaning: "too much". Only the politeness changes.

Casual

New Atashin'chi · Episode 2

もう！しみちゃん、笑わらいすぎ。

"Geez! Shimi-chan, you're laughing way too much."

～すぎる means too much: more than is good. It goes on the verb's ます-stem (笑います → 笑い + すぎる), on an い-adjective without い (高い → 高すぎる), or on a な-adjective as it is (静か → 静かすぎる).

On this card, she's on the phone and Shimi-chan won't stop laughing. In casual speech the る often drops, like here: 笑いすぎ.

Polite

Mob Psycho 100 · Episode 3

細こまかすぎますよ 志村しむらさん

"You're being too picky, Shimura."

すぎます is the polite すぎる. On this card, 細かい drops the い and adds すぎます: "too fussy about details".

Examples

The morning after a big dinner, a coworker asks why you look tired.

ゆうべ、食たべすぎました。

"I ate too much last night."

食べます → 食べ + すぎます.

Polite

In a shop, you put the bag back on the shelf.

このかばんは高たかすぎます。

"This bag is too expensive."

い-adjective: drop the い. 高い → 高すぎる.

Polite

You and a friend walk into an empty café.

ここ、静しずかすぎない？

"Isn't it a bit too quiet in here?"

な-adjective: just add すぎる. 静か → 静かすぎる.

Casual

You wake up and look at the clock.

やばい、寝ねすぎた！

"Oh no, I overslept!"

すぎる changes like a る-verb: すぎた, すぎない, すぎて.

Casual

With and without

Without

この靴くつは高たかい。

"These shoes are expensive." Maybe you still buy them.

With すぎる

この靴くつは高たかすぎる。

"These shoes are too expensive." You won't buy them.

Sentence mining

Polite

Quartet · Episode 3

ちょっと条件じょうけんが厳きびしすぎません？

"Aren't the rules a bit too strict?"

厳しい ("strict") → 厳し + すぎません.

Polite

Legal High · Episode 6

服部はっとりさん。　詳くわし過すぎます。

"Hattori-san. That's far too detailed."

詳しい ("detailed") → 詳し + 過ぎます. 過ぎる is すぎる in kanji.

Polite

Sailor Suit and Machine Gun · Episode 2

頑張がんばりすぎるんですよ 組長くみちょうは

"You push yourself too hard, boss."

頑張ります → 頑張り + すぎる. 組長: the head of the gang.

Polite

Weakest Beast · Episode 2

こっちも 焼やき過すぎちゃいました

"I overcooked this one too."

焼きます ("grill, bake") → 焼き + 過ぎる. ちゃいました: "ended up (oops)".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 1

僕ぼく、張はり切きり過すぎてて、途中とちゅうでばてちゃった。

"I got too excited and wore myself out halfway."

張り切る ("be all fired up") → 張り切り + 過ぎる. ばてる: to run out of energy.

Casual

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 1

うん…　飲のみ過すぎちゃって

"Yeah... I drank too much."

飲みます → 飲み + 過ぎる.

Casual

Overprotected Kahoko · Episode 1

昔むかしから甘あますぎるんだよ

"You've always been too soft on her."

甘い ("sweet", here "soft, lenient") → 甘 + すぎる.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 18

怖こわすぎるね…

"That's way too scary."

怖い drops い, adds すぎる.

Reference

A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

N5 Grammar

～く・～に (Adverbs)

Polite

YouTube · video

バッテリーが、今こん本当ほんとうに早はやくなくなります。

"The battery runs out really fast now."

く turns an い-adjective into a word that describes the action: 早い (fast) → 早く (fast, quickly). Drop the い, add く.

On this card, it answers "How does it run out?": fast. 本当に (really) is the same trick on a noun: 本当 + に.

な-adjectives take に instead: 静か → 静かに (quietly). Politeness comes from the verb at the end, here なくなります.

Casual

YouTube · video

へえ。もうなんか、普通ふつうにスーパーで、適当てきとうにいつも買かってた。

"Huh. I always just grabbed them at the supermarket without thinking."

The な-adjective version, with に: 適当 (random, whatever) → 適当に (without much thought). 普通 (normal) → 普通に (just, normally).

Examples

Your friend is walking way too slowly.

早はやく来きて！

"Come on, hurry!"

早い ("early, fast") → 早く = "quickly". 来て: "come!".

Casual

A sign in a library.

静しずかにしてください。

"Please be quiet."

静か ("quiet") → 静かに = "quietly". 静かにする: "be quiet".

Polite

A kid shows you their drawing.

上手じょうずに描えがけたね。

"You drew that really well."

上手 ("skillful") → 上手に = "well". 描けた: "could draw".

Casual

At the hairdresser.

髪かみを短みじかく切きってください。

"Please cut my hair short."

短い ("short") → 短く = "short", saying how to cut it.

Polite

Someone asks how you slept.

昨日きのうはよく寝ねた。

"I slept well last night."

いい ("good") → よく = "well". いい is the odd one: its く form comes from 良い.

Casual

With and without

Without

静しずかな部屋へやです。

"It's a quiet room." 静かな describes the room, a noun.

With に

静しずかに話はなしてください。

"Please talk quietly." 静かに describes how you talk.

Sentence mining

Polite

Source unknown No source

このゲームは簡単かんたんに言いうと、間違まちがい探さがしですね。

"Put simply, this game is spot the difference."

簡単に言うと = "to put it simply".

Polite

Source unknown No source

猫ねこの毛けを、丁寧ていねいに梳すくのが好すきです。

"I like brushing the cat's fur carefully."

丁寧 (careful) → 丁寧に.

Polite

Legal High · Episode 1

非常ひじょうに静しずかなものでした。

"It was very quiet."

非常 + に turns it into "extremely". It tells you how quiet.

Casual

Overprotected Kahoko · Episode 10

遅おそくなって ごめん。

"Sorry I'm late."

遅い becomes 遅く before なる: "became late".

Casual

Sailor Suit and Machine Gun · Episode 4

早はやく行いって！

"Go, quickly!"

早い becomes 早く to say how to go.

Casual

Source unknown No source

炭すみ治郎みたいに、速はやく歩あるけないでしょう？

"You can't walk as fast as Tanjiro, right?"

速い ("fast") → 速く = "fast". 歩けない: "can't walk".

Casual

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 3

結構けっこう きれいにしてるんだね。

"You keep it pretty clean, huh."

きれい is a な-adjective, so it takes に: きれいにする, "make it clean".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 8

そんな簡単かんたんに諦あきらめんな！

"Don't give up so easily!"

簡単 + に tells you how. 諦めんな is a rough 諦めるな.

N5 Grammar

より・～の方が

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 6

まっ、コーヒーより、ウイスキーのほうが多おおかったかもな。

"Well, maybe there was more whiskey in it than coffee."

より means than, and の方が marks the one that's more: ウイスキーの方が多い = the whiskey is more.

Put より right after the thing you compare against: コーヒーより (than coffee). On this card, the sentence answers "Which was more?": the whiskey.

Each half works alone too: コーヒーより多い, or ウイスキーの方が多い. 方 is often written ほう. Politeness comes from the end: 多かったです.

Polite

YouTube · video

思おもったより早はやく、クイーンズタウンの街まちにつきそうですね。

"Looks like we'll reach Queenstown sooner than I thought."

より means "than". On this card, 思ったより ("than I thought") + 早く ("sooner"), and つきそうですね = "looks like we'll arrive".

Examples

Choosing a drink with a friend.

コーヒーより紅茶こうちゃの方ほうが好すき。

"I like tea more than coffee."

Casual

Comparing cities with a coworker.

東京とうきょうは大阪おおさかより大おおきいです。

"Tokyo is bigger than Osaka."

Only より here: Tokyo is already the topic.

Polite

A friend asks: bus or train?

電車でんしゃの方ほうが早はやいよ。

"The train's faster."

Only の方が: the other one is clear.

Casual

Holding two bags in a shop.

どちらの方ほうが軽かるいですか。

"Which one is lighter?"

どちらの方が...? = which one is more...?

Polite

With and without

Without

ウイスキーが多おおい。

"There's a lot of whiskey." No comparison.

With より・の方が

コーヒーよりウイスキーの方ほうが多おおい。

"There's more whiskey than coffee." Now it's a comparison.

Sentence mining

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 10

はい、いつもより多おおめに、ゴロゴロしま～す。

"Okay, I'll laze around more than usual!"

いつもより = than usual.

Polite

YouTube · video

そうですね...長ながめの方ほうが好すきですか？

"I see... do you prefer them longer?"

方が好き = like more, prefer.

Polite

YouTube · video

でも、とにかく、僕ぼくは朝あさの方ほうが頭あたまが動うごきます。

"Anyway, my brain works better in the morning."

Casual

Weakest Beast · Episode 3

私わたしより高たかいよ。

"You're worth more than me."

私 ("me") + より + 高い ("expensive") = "you're worth more than me". Literally "more expensive than me".

Casual

Source unknown No source

東北とうほくの地震じしんより揺ゆれたわ。

"That shook more than the Tohoku earthquake."

Casual

Source unknown No source

え？明あかるいほうが、よくない？

"Huh? Isn't brighter better?"

After an adjective it's just 方が, no の.

Casual

Daily Lives of High School Boys · Episode 6

あの人ひとは俺おれよりバカなんだよ。

"She's dumber than me."

俺 ("me") + より + バカ ("stupid") = "dumber than me". なんだよ: explaining, a bit fed up.
