N5 Grammar

一番 (いちばん)

Polite

Comprehensible Japanese · これ、それ、あれ、どれ

これが一番いちばん大おおきい松まつぼっくりです。

"This is the biggest pine cone."

一番 means "number one". Put it right before an adjective and it means the most: 一番 + 大きい = "the biggest".

On this card, out of all the pine cones, this one wins. The sentence answers "Which one is the biggest?": これ.

一番 is the same in polite and casual speech. The politeness comes from the end: です here, だ or nothing with friends.

Casual

I am Mita, Your Housekeeper · Episode 3

結も世界せかいで一番いちばん好すきだよ。

"I love you more than anyone in the world too, Yui."

一番 goes right before the word it makes "most". On this card, 世界で ("in the world") + 一番 + 好き ("like") = "love you most in the world".

Examples

Showing a friend a family photo.

家族かぞくの中なかで、父ちちが一番いちばん背せが高たかいです。

"In my family, my dad is the tallest."

X の中で = "among X". It sets the group, then 一番 picks the winner.

Polite

A friend asks about the seasons in Japan.

秋あきが一番いちばん好すきです。

"I like autumn the most."

一番好き = "favorite". Very common.

Polite

Looking at three cakes in a bakery window.

どれが一番いちばんおいしい？

"Which one is the tastiest?"

Question word + が + 一番. Use どれ for three or more things.

Casual

A kid asks about mountains.

日本にほんで一番いちばん高たかい山やまは富士ふじ山やまだよ。

"The tallest mountain in Japan is Mt. Fuji."

Place + で sets the area: "in Japan".

Casual

With and without

Without

この部屋へやは広ひろいです。

"This room is big." Just a description, no comparison.

With 一番

この部屋へやが一番いちばん広ひろいです。

"This room is the biggest." Now it beats all the other rooms.

Notice は turns into が. With 一番 you're picking one thing out of a group, and が is the particle for "this one, not the others".

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

ちなみに、名古屋なごやで一番いちばん有名ゆうめいなのはたぶん名古屋なごや城じょうです。

"By the way, the most famous thing in Nagoya is probably Nagoya Castle."

名古屋で = "in Nagoya", the area. 一番有名 = "most famous".

Polite

YouTube · video

ここをまっすぐ行いったところに、僕ぼくが一番いちばん好すきな写真しゃしんスポットがあります。

"Straight ahead from here is my favorite photo spot."

一番好きな + noun = "my favorite ___". 好き is a な-adjective, so it needs な before a noun.

Polite

When Marnie Was There

いいえ、本人ほんにんに聞きくのが一番いちばんです。

"No, asking her yourself is best."

本人に聞く ("asking the person herself") + のが + 一番 = "asking her is best". の turns the verb into a thing.

Casual

YouTube · video

私わたしは一番いちばん下した。

"I'm the youngest."

一番 works with position words too: 一番下 = "the very bottom", here the youngest sibling.

Casual

Overprotected Kahoko · Episode 9

ここが 一番いちばんいいわね。

"This place is the best."

ここ ("this place") + が + 一番いい ("the best") = "this place is the best". わね: soft, feminine.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 17

お前まえがいちばん働はたらいたからな。

"You worked the most, after all."

いちばん goes before the verb here.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 47

いちばんコクがあるっす。

"This one has the richest flavor."

っす is a rough, casual です.

Reference

N5 Grammar

とても

Polite

Comprehensible Japanese · A Day in my Life in Sendai

この自転じてん車しゃは、電気でんきの力ちからで動うごくので、とても快適かいてきです。

"This bike runs on electric power, so it's very comfortable."

とても means very. It goes right before the describing word: とても + 快適 = "very comfortable".

On this card, the electric bike answers "how comfortable?" with "a lot". Without とても, 快適です is just "it's comfortable".

とても itself never changes. Polite or casual only shows at the end: とても快適です / とても快適だ.

Casual

I am Mita, Your Housekeeper · Episode 8

とてもいいと思おもうな、あの家族かぞく。

"I think that family is really nice."

とても goes before the word it makes stronger. On this card, とても + いい ("good") = "really nice", and the topic, あの家族 ("that family"), comes at the end as an afterthought.

Examples

Small talk with a neighbour on a winter morning.

今日きょうはとても寒さむいですね。

"It's very cold today, isn't it."

Polite

Someone asks what your hometown is like.

とても静しずかな町まちです。

"It's a very quiet town."

Before a noun, とても still sits in front of the describing word: とても静かな + 町.

Polite

You get home after a long day of moving boxes.

とても疲つかれた。

"I'm really tired."

とても also works with feeling words that are verbs: 疲れる, 困る, 驚く.

Casual

A friend lets you try their curry.

とってもおいしい！

"Super tasty!"

とても sounds a little neat. With friends, people often say とっても (warmer, stronger) or すごく instead.

Casual

With and without

Without

この本ほんは面白おもしろいです。

"This book is interesting." A plain fact.

With とても

この本ほんはとても面白おもしろいです。

"This book is very interesting." You really mean it.

Sentence mining

Polite

Comprehensible Japanese · My Five Favorite Things

とってもおすすめです。

"I really recommend it."

とっても is the warmer, stronger way to say とても.

Polite

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 9

正直しょうじき、とても残念ざんねんです。

"Honestly, it's very disappointing."

とても + 残念 ("disappointing, a shame") = "very disappointing". 正直: "honestly".

Polite

Legal High · Episode 2

やっぱり とても悲かなしいです。

"It really is very sad."

とても + 悲しい ("sad") = "very sad". やっぱり: "after all, really".

Polite

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 2

とっても大切たいせつなことなんですよ。

"It's a very important thing."

とっても is とても with extra feeling.

Polite

Overprotected Kahoko · Episode 2

逆ぎゃくの場合ばあいは とっても悲かなしいんで

"When it's the other way round, it's very sad."

とっても + 悲しい ("sad").

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 22

ありがとう、とっても嬉うれしい！

"Thank you, I'm so happy!"

とっても is a warmer とても.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 16

当あたりはずれがとても大おおきい。

"It's very hit or miss."

とても + an adjective.

N5 Grammar

ちょっと

Casual

He Who Can't Marry · Episode 1

うーんこれはちょっと細ほそいから厳密げんみつにはスパゲティーニ

"Hmm, this one's a bit thin, so strictly speaking it's spaghettini."

ちょっと means a little, a bit. It goes right before the part it makes smaller: ちょっと + 細い = "a bit thin".

On this card, he looks at the pasta and says it's a bit too thin to be spaghetti, so strictly it's spaghettini. Without ちょっと it would just be "it's thin".

Japanese also use ちょっと to soften things: ちょっと待って (wait a sec), or 今日はちょっと… to say no gently. ちょっと never changes; polite or casual only shows at the end.

Polite

YouTube · video

ファミリーマートの卵たまごサンドはパッケージがなんかちょっと小ちいさいですね。

"The FamilyMart egg sandwich package is kind of a bit small."

ちょっと softens the word right after it. On this card, ちょっと + 小さいですね = "a bit small", and なんか is just "kind of".

Examples

You try on a jacket in a shop. Your friend asks how it fits.

ちょっと大おおきい。

"It's a bit big."

Casual

At a restaurant, the waiter asks how the curry is.

ちょっと辛つらいです。

"It's a little spicy."

Polite

Your friend is about to leave, but you still need your shoes on.

ちょっと待まって！

"Wait a sec!"

Here ちょっと isn't really "a little". It just makes 待って softer.

Casual

A coworker asks if you want to go drinking tonight. You don't.

今日きょうはちょっと…。

"Today's a bit…"

The rest is left unsaid. Everyone understands it as a soft no.

Polite

With and without

Plain

この靴くつは大おおきい。

"These shoes are big."

With ちょっと

この靴くつはちょっと大おおきい。

"These shoes are a bit big."

Plain

待まって！

"Wait!" Short and sharp.

With ちょっと

ちょっと待まって！

"Wait a sec!" Same request, softer.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

あの〜、自転じてん車しゃを漕こぎながら地図ちずを見みるのはちょっと危あぶないですね。

"Um, looking at a map while riding a bike is a bit dangerous."

ちょっと + 危ない: a bit dangerous. It also keeps the warning gentle.

Polite

YouTube · video

明日あしたもうちょっと長野ながの県けんの北きたの方ほうに行いきます。

"Tomorrow I'm going a bit further north in Nagano."

もうちょっと is "a bit more": a bit further north.

Polite

YouTube · video

ここは多分たぶんちょっと動画どうがを撮とってはいけませんね。

"We probably can't really film here."

The softening ちょっと: it makes "not allowed" sound less blunt.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 3

ちょっとお手本てほん見みせてよ

"Come on, show me how it's done."

The softening ちょっと: it makes the request sound lighter.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 6

クマ野郎やろうちょっと焼やいてこいよ

"Hey, you bear, go get yourself a bit of a tan."

ちょっと + 焼いてこい: go tan a bit. Rough, teasing talk between friends.

Casual

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 5

ちょっと待まって！

"Wait a sec!"

ちょっと softens it: "wait a little", not a hard order.

Casual

Weakest Beast · Episode 2

ちょっと 近ちかい！

"You're a bit too close!"

ちょっと + 近い: "a bit close", a soft way to complain.

N5 Grammar

たくさん

Polite

YouTube · video

今日きょうは、今いまからアジをたくさん釣つりたいですね。

"Today I want to catch lots of horse mackerel [starting now]."

たくさん means a lot: a big amount or a big number of something. Put it right before the verb (たくさん釣る, "catch a lot"), or before a noun with の (たくさんの魚, "lots of fish").

On this card, he's getting his bait ready and says how many fish he wants: たくさん.

たくさん itself never changes. Polite or casual only shows at the end: たくさん釣りたいです / たくさん釣りたい.

Casual

I am Mita, Your Housekeeper · Episode 9

野菜やさいもたくさん食たべるんだぞ

"Make sure you eat lots of vegetables too."

たくさん goes right before the verb and means "a lot". On this card, たくさん食べる = "eat a lot", and んだぞ makes it a firm, fatherly instruction.

Examples

Monday morning, a coworker asks about your weekend.

週末しゅうまつはたくさん寝ねました。

"I slept a lot over the weekend."

たくさん is about how much. For "very" with a describing word, it's とても: とても眠い, "very sleepy".

Polite

Telling a friend about the town festival.

お祭まつりにたくさんの人ひとが来きました。

"Lots of people came to the festival."

Right before a noun, add の: たくさんの + 人.

Polite

Your roommate wants to go shopping. You check the fridge first.

卵たまご、まだたくさんあるよ。

"We still have lots of eggs."

Very common spot: ～が たくさん ある / いる, "there are lots of ___".

Casual

Back from a trip, a friend asks if you took pictures.

うん、たくさん撮とったよ！

"Yeah, I took loads!"

Casual

With and without

Without

水みずを飲のみました。

"I drank water." Just what you did.

With たくさん

水みずをたくさん飲のみました。

"I drank a lot of water." Now you say how much.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · Let's learn Japanese while walking to Asakusa!!

たくさんの自転じてん車しゃが駐輪ちゅうりんされています。

"Lots of bikes are parked here."

たくさんの + 自転車 ("bikes"). 駐輪: parking a bike.

Polite

Source unknown No source

タンポポがたくさんあります。

"There are lots of dandelions."

～がたくさんあります: "there are lots of ___".

Polite

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 2

私わたし お話はなししたいことが たくさんあるんです

"There's so much I want to tell you."

お話ししたいこと: "things I want to talk about". たくさんある: there are lots of them.

Polite

The Journalist · Episode 3

たくさんのことを 教おしえていただきました

"You taught me a lot."

たくさんのこと: "lots of things". 教えていただきました is a very polite "you taught me".

Casual

Source unknown No source

このビーチ、石いしころがたくさんあるね。

"This beach has lots of pebbles, huh."

石ころ: small stones, pebbles.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 20

わぁ～！たくさんあるね。

"Wow! There are so many."

たくさん goes before the verb.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 23

すごくたくさん入はいったわ。

"A whole lot fit in."

すごく makes たくさん even bigger.

Reference

A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

N5 Grammar

けっこう (結構)

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 6

えっ、ストロング？結構けっこう、苦にがいよ。

"Huh, the strong one? It's pretty bitter, you know."

けっこう means quite, pretty: more than you'd expect, but softer than とても. It goes right before the describing word: 結構 + 苦い = "pretty bitter".

On this card, someone picks the strong one and gets a warning: it's more bitter than they might think.

結構です has a second job: a polite "No, thank you" when someone offers you something.

Polite

Quartet · Episode 2

僕ぼくは結構けっこうです

"I'm fine, thanks."

結構です is also a polite "no thanks". On this card, 僕は結構です = "none for me": the others can have some.

Examples

First time trying natto. Your host asks how it is.

納豆なっとう、けっこうおいしいです。

"Natto is actually pretty good."

けっこう often carries "more than I thought". You expected worse.

Polite

At the convenience store checkout.

A: 袋ふくろはいりますか。
B: いえ、結構けっこうです。

A: "Do you need a bag?" B: "No, I'm fine."

結構です here means "no thanks". The いえ in front makes it clear.

Polite

Halfway up a hill on a long walk with a friend.

けっこう歩あるいたね。

"We've walked quite a lot."

With a verb, けっこう means "quite a lot".

Casual

Looking at a flat with a friend.

この部屋へや、けっこう広ひろいね。

"This room is pretty big."

Casual

With and without

Without

この映画えいがは面白おもしろかった。

"This movie was interesting." A plain opinion.

With けっこう

この映画えいがはけっこう面白おもしろかった。

"This movie was pretty interesting." Better than you expected.

YouTube · video

結構けっこう、エンジニアにも人気にんきのブランドっすよね。

"It's a brand that's pretty popular with engineers too, right?"

結構 + 人気 ("popular"). っす is a relaxed way to say です.

"No, thank you. Sorry."

結構です: "no thanks".

I am Mita, Your Housekeeper · Episode 3

いえ 結構けっこうです

"No, I'm fine."

The classic polite refusal: いえ + 結構です.

加か穂ほ子こ 結構けっこう お酒さけ強つよいみたい

"How is it? Does it suit me pretty well?"

N5 Grammar

あまり～ない

Polite

YouTube · video

でも日本にほんは地理ちり的てきな条件じょうけんで、あまりバナナを作つくっていません。

"But because of its geography, Japan doesn't grow many bananas."

あまり + a negative means not very, not much. あまり goes before the part it's about, and the sentence has to end negative: 作っていません, not 作っています.

On this card, the sentence answers "Does Japan grow bananas?": some, but not many. Without あまり it would be "Japan doesn't grow bananas" at all.

あまり itself never changes. Polite or casual shows at the end: あまり作っていません / あまり作ってない. In speech it's often あんまり.

Casual

Overprotected Kahoko · Episode 7

私わたしも糸いとのこと あんまり好すきじゃない

"I don't really like you either, Ito."

あんまり is the everyday casual form of あまり, and it still needs a negative after it. On this card, あんまり + 好きじゃない = "don't really like".

Examples

A friend asks if the movie was good.

あまり面白おもしろくない。

"It's not that interesting."

面白い → 面白くない. あまり needs that ない.

Casual

A coworker asks if you drink.

あまり飲のみません。

"I don't drink much."

Polite

Your friend asks if you're hungry.

あんまりお腹なか空あいてない。

"I'm not that hungry."

あんまり is the spoken way to say あまり.

Casual

The teacher asks if you understood the explanation.

あまり分わかりません。

"I didn't really understand."

Polite

With and without

Plain

このケーキは甘あまくない。

"This cake isn't sweet." Not at all.

With あまり

このケーキはあまり甘あまくない。

"This cake isn't very sweet." A little, not much.

Polite

このケーキはあまり甘あまくないです。

Same meaning, polite.

Not this

このケーキはあまり甘あまい。

あまり needs a negative at the end. Without it the sentence breaks.

Polite

YouTube · video

あまり急きゅうじゃないからハイキングも本当ほんとうに簡単かんたんで、普通ふつうの服ふくで来くることができます。

"It's not very steep, so the hike is really easy and you can come in normal clothes."

急 (steep) + じゃない. あまり works with な-adjectives too.

Polite

あまり + ない: not much nature.

"I don't watch dubbed movies much."

見る → 見ない. Adding です makes it polite.

Source unknown No source

だからボウリング場じょうに、僕ぼくの足あしのサイズのシューズがあんまりないです。

"So bowling alleys don't have many shoes in my size."

あんまり, the spoken version.

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 9

あんまり変かわりませんね。

"It doesn't really change."

あんまり is the everyday あまり, still with a negative.

あまり + ない (there isn't): not many places.

The ない is left unsaid. あんまり alone already tells you where it's going.

N5 Grammar

全然～ない

Casual

YouTube · video

とにかく最初さいしょは漫画まんがの作つくり方かたも全然ぜんぜん知しらなくって

"Anyway, at first I didn't know anything about how to make manga either."

全然 (ぜんぜん) + a negative means not at all. It goes before the part it's about, and the sentence ends negative: 知らない, not 知る.

On this card, the sentence answers "Did you know how manga is made?": no, nothing. It's the strong version of あまり: あまり知らない is "don't know much", 全然知らない is "don't know at all".

全然 never changes. Polite or casual shows at the end: 全然知りません / 全然知らない. In everyday talk you'll also hear 全然大丈夫 ("totally fine"): no negative, but it still answers a worry with "not at all".

Polite

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 5

全然ぜんぜん 知しりませんでした。

"I had no idea."

全然 + a negative = "not at all". On this card, 全然 + 知りませんでした ("didn't know") = "had no idea at all".

Examples

A friend asks if you slept well before the exam.

全然ぜんぜん寝ねてない。

"I didn't sleep at all."

Casual

A coworker asks if you speak Korean.

全然ぜんぜん話はなせません。

"I can't speak it at all."

Polite

Your friend shows you a math problem.

全然ぜんぜん分わからない。

"I have no idea."

Casual

A coworker apologizes for being five minutes late.

全然ぜんぜん大丈夫だいじょうぶですよ。

"It's totally fine."

The everyday 全然: no negative, but it answers "Is it a problem?" with "not at all".

Polite

With and without

With あまり

あまり分わからない。

"I don't really understand." A little, not much.

With 全然

全然ぜんぜん分わからない。

"I don't understand at all." Nothing.

Polite

全然ぜんぜん分わかりません。

Same meaning, polite.

Not this

全然ぜんぜん分わかる。

全然 needs a negative (or 大丈夫). Without it the sentence breaks.

Polite

Source unknown No source

だから全然ぜんぜん雰囲気ふんいきが違ちがいますね。

"So the atmosphere is completely different."

違う (to be different) works like a negative: not the same at all.

Casual

YouTube · video

もう顔かおもほぼすっぴんなんであの全然ぜんぜん

"My face is basically bare anyway, so, um, not at all."

The rest is left unsaid. 全然 alone means "not at all, no problem".

Casual

Source unknown No source

"I just don't get this idea of only ever doing one job."

分かんない is the spoken 分からない. 全然 + that: don't get it at all.

Casual

全然ぜんぜん 眠ねむれなかった。

"I couldn't sleep at all."

全然 + 眠れなかった ("couldn't sleep") = "couldn't sleep at all".

Casual

全然 + 食べてない ("haven't eaten") = "not eating at all". し: "and besides".

"We're not catching anything at all."

全然 + a negative verb.

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 17

"It's completely different."

違う works like a negative here: not the same.

N5 Grammar

いつも・よく・時々

Polite

YouTube · video

いつも持もち歩あるいています。

"I always carry it with me."

いつも (always), よく (often) and 時々 (ときどき, sometimes) say how often something happens. They go before the action: いつも + 持ち歩いています.

On this card, the sentence answers "How often do you carry it?": every time. Without いつも it would just be "I carry it".

They never change. Polite or casual only shows at the end: いつも持ち歩いています / いつも持ち歩いてる.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 28

いつも持もち歩あるいてるの。

"I always carry it around."

いつも means every time, and goes before the verb. On this card, 持ち歩いてる is the casual 持ち歩いている ("carry around").

Examples

A friend asks what you have for breakfast.

いつもパン。

"Always bread."

Casual

The café owner says they've seen you before.

よく来きます。

"I come here often."

Polite

A friend asks if you cook.

時々ときどき作つくる。

"Sometimes."

Casual

A coworker asks if you watch Japanese TV.

時々ときどきドラマを見みます。

"I watch dramas sometimes."

Polite

With and without

Always

いつも歩あるいて行いきます。

"I always walk there."

Often

よく歩あるいて行いきます。

"I often walk there."

Sometimes

時々ときどき歩あるいて行いきます。

"I sometimes walk there."

Not often

あまり歩あるいて行いきません。

"I don't walk there much." あまり needs a negative at the end.

Polite

YouTube · video

母ははは私わたしはいつも少すこし変かわっていると思おもっていました

"My mother always thought I was a bit odd."

いつも + 変わっている: always a bit different.

Polite

Source unknown No source

僕ぼくは本屋ほんやさんで、よく立たち読よみをします。

"I often read standing up in bookstores."

立ち読み is reading in a shop without buying.

Polite

Source unknown No source

私わたしたちはメッセージに絵え文字もじをよく使つかいます。

"We often use emoji in messages."

よく can also sit right before the verb, after the object.

Polite

Source unknown No source

まあ、たまに食たべます。

"Well, I eat it now and then."

たまに is "now and then", a bit rarer than 時々.

Casual

New Atashin'chi · Episode 2

昔むかしよくギンナン拾ひろったねえ。

"We used to pick ginkgo nuts a lot, didn't we?"

昔 (back then) + よく: something you did often in the past.

Casual

Source unknown No source

お弁当べんとうもいつも豪華ごうかでうまそうで。

"And his bento is always so fancy and tasty-looking."

いつも + 豪華: always fancy. It works with describing words too.

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 15

"They're often lying around."

よく = often.

N5 Grammar

もう

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 3

ユーカリ？　かわいく食たべてますけど、もう、あれ限界げんかいです。

"Eucalyptus? He looks cute eating it, but he's [already] at his limit."

もう means already: the change has happened, sooner than you'd think. It goes before the part it's about: もう + 限界 = "already at the limit".

On this card, it answers "has it happened yet?" with "yes, already". He looks fine, but he's done.

もう itself never changes. Polite or casual only shows at the end: もう限界です / もう限界だ.

Casual

YouTube · video

もう着火ちゃっか剤ざいない。着火ちゃっか剤ざいはない。

"We're out of fire starters. There are no fire starters."

With a negative at the end, もう becomes not anymore: there were some before, now they're gone.

Examples

Your friend offers to cook you dinner.

もう食たべた。

"I already ate."

Casual

You look at the clock at a party.

あ、もう11時じですね。

"Oh, it's already 11."

Polite

Someone asks if you still live in Osaka.

もう住すんでいません。

"I don't live there anymore."

Polite

After the third slice of cake.

もう食たべられない。

"I can't eat any more."

Casual

With and without

Without

宿題しゅくだいをした。

"I did my homework." Just a fact.

With もう

もう宿題しゅくだいをした。

"I already did my homework." It's done, no need to ask.

Without

お金かねがない。

"I have no money." Maybe never had any.

With もう

もうお金かねがない。

"I have no money left." There was some, now it's gone.

Polite

YouTube · video

前まえは、ここからゴキブリが出でてきたんですけど、もう最近さいきんは大丈夫だいじょうぶですね。

"Cockroaches used to come out of here, but lately it's fine now."

前は (before) vs もう (now): the problem is over.

Casual

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 1

"She's already 30, but..."

もう + 30 = "already 30". のに: "and yet", she's old enough to know better.

"Just go home."

もう + 帰れ ("go home!", an order) = "enough, just go home". With an order, もう means "that's it".

"That's enough."

もう + 十分 ("enough") = "that's already enough".

Mob Psycho 100 · Episode 10

もう 無理むり。

"I can't anymore."

もう + 無理 ("impossible") = "I can't anymore". もう here means "anymore".

Mob Psycho 100 · Episode 6

"Just give up already."

もう + 諦めろ ("give up!") = "just give up already".

もう + そんな時間 ("that time") = "is it that late already?". Sooner than expected.

"It's already summer."

N5 Grammar

まだ

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 10

まだ眠ねむいよ、もうちょっと寝ねよう。

"I'm still sleepy, let's sleep a bit more."

まだ means still: something hasn't changed yet. It goes before the word it's about: まだ + 眠い = "still sleepy".

On this card, it answers "is it over yet?" with "no, it's still going". Sleepy before, sleepy now.

まだ itself never changes. Polite or casual only shows at the end: まだ眠いよ / まだ眠いです.

Polite

YouTube · video

今いまのところ、僕ぼくはまだ動物どうぶつを見みていません。

"So far, I haven't seen any animals yet."

With a negative at the end, まだ becomes not yet: it hasn't happened, but it still might. Here: no animals so far, maybe later.

Examples

Your friend checks if you're ready to leave.

まだ食たべてる。

"I'm still eating."

Casual

The waiter asks if you've decided.

すみません、まだです。

"Sorry, not yet."

まだです on its own is a full answer: "not yet". Casual: まだ。

Polite

Someone asks if the shop is open at 9 pm.

まだ開ひらいていますよ。

"It's still open."

Polite

A friend asks if you've seen the new movie.

まだ見みてない。

"I haven't seen it yet."

"Haven't yet" uses ～ていない (casual ～てない), not just ない. 見ない would mean "I won't watch it".

Casual

With and without

Without

雨あめが降ふっている。

"It's raining." Just what's happening now.

With まだ

まだ雨あめが降ふっている。

"It's still raining." It was raining before, and it hasn't stopped.

Without

宿題しゅくだいをしていない。

"I haven't done my homework." Sounds like you might not do it at all.

With まだ

まだ宿題しゅくだいをしていない。

"I haven't done my homework yet." You plan to.

Polite

YouTube · video

"I just woke up, so I'm still a bit sleepy."

Polite

YouTube · video

小屋こやの制作せいさくはまだ続つづいています。

"Work on the cabin is still going on."

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 4

まだ大学だいがく生せいです。

"I'm still in college."

まだ + 大学生 ("college student") = "still a college student". With a noun, まだ means "still".

Polite

"It's still only Monday."

まだ + 月曜 ("Monday") = "still only Monday". なんで: "so, you see".

"Phew, my heart's still pounding."

The scary part is over, but the feeling hasn't gone yet.

ううん、まだ。

ううん ("no") + まだ = "not yet". まだ alone is a full answer.

N5 Grammar

ます

Polite

YouTube · video

ここに、お湯ゆを入いれます。

"[You] pour hot water in here."

ます goes on the end of a verb and makes it polite. 入れる (to put in) becomes 入れます. The meaning stays the same.

On this card, someone shows how to use something, step by step. The sentence answers "What do I do?".

Past: 入れました (put in). Not: 入れません (don't put in).

Examples

A coworker asks what you're doing this weekend.

京都きょうとに行いきます。

"I'm going to Kyoto."

行く becomes 行き + ます. The last sound changes from u to i before ます.

Polite

The waiter asks if you liked the curry. The plate is empty.

全部ぜんぶ食たべました。

"I ate it all."

ました is the past of ます: 食べます (eat) → 食べました (ate).

Polite

Your host offers you a beer. You're driving.

お酒さけは飲のみません。

"I don't drink alcohol."

ません is the "not" of ます: 飲みます (drink) → 飲みません (don't drink).

Polite

A client asks when you'll get to the office tomorrow.

9時じに来きます。

"I'll come at 9."

来る → 来ます, read きます. ます covers "will" too: no separate future form.

Polite

With and without

Without ます

毎朝まいあさコーヒーを飲のむ。

"I drink coffee every morning." The verb as it is in the dictionary.

With ます

毎朝まいあさコーヒーを飲のみます。

Same meaning, now polite. For people you don't know well, at work, in shops.

ru-verbs

食たべる → 食たべます

Ends in える or いる: take off る, add ます. 見る → 見ます.

u-verbs

飲のむ → 飲のみます

The last u sound turns into i, then ます. 待つ → 待ちます, 帰る → 帰ります.

The two odd ones

する → します　来くる → 来きます

来ます is read きます.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

ちょっと厳選げんせんします。

"I'll be a bit picky."

厳選する is "to choose carefully". する becomes します. ます also covers the future: "I'll do it".

Polite

YouTube · video

成田なりた空港くうこうで食たべました。

"I ate it at Narita Airport."

ました is the past: 食べます → 食べました.

Polite

YouTube · video

このエリアに異常いじょうはありません。

"There's nothing wrong in this area."

ある (there is) → あります → ありません (there isn't). 異常 is "something abnormal".

Polite

YouTube · video

予約よやくが完了かんりょうしました。

"The reservation is complete."

完了する (to be completed) → 完了します → 完了しました.

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 22

それでは営業えいぎょう会議かいぎを始はじめます

"Well then, let's start the sales meeting."

始める → 始めます. る drops, ます goes on.

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 20

おじゃまします

"Sorry to intrude." [entering someone's home]

じゃまする ("to get in the way") + ます. A set phrase when you walk into someone's place.

Polite

Border · Episode 9

はい 仕事しごとで行いきました

"Yes, I went for work."

行きます → 行きました: the polite past.

Polite

Polite verb + rising voice is already a question, no か needed.

Polite Form and Verb Stems · Using 「～ます」 to make verbs polite

N5 Grammar

る-Verb (Dictionary)

Polite～ます drop る, add ます
Casual～る dictionary form

Same meaning. Only the politeness changes.

Japanese has three types of verbs. This page is about the second one, the る-verbs.

Verb typeDictionaryPolite
1う-verbmost verbs書くalso 飲む, 話す, 買う...書きますu sound → i sound, add ます
2る-verbthis page食べるalso 見る, 起きる, 寝る...食べますdrop る, add ます
3Irregularjust these two verbsする
来る		します
来ますjust learn these
How to tell which type a verb is
  1. Step 1

    Is it する or 来る?

    Yes: Irregular. No: go to step 2.

  2. Step 2

    Does it end in る?

    No: う-verb (書く, 飲む). Yes: go to step 3.

  3. Step 3

    Is the sound just before る an i or an e?

    No: う-verb (分かる wa-ka-ru, 作る tsu-ku-ru).

    Yes: usually a る-verb (見る mi-ru, 食べる ta-be-ru).

A few break step 3. These look like る-verbs but are う-verbs: 帰る, 入る, 走る, 知る.

る-verbs are the second big group of Japanese verbs. Their dictionary form always ends in る, and the sound right before it is an i or an e sound: 見る (miru), 食べる (taberu).

In Japanese they're called 一段 (ichidan), "one step": the front of the verb never changes. To use one, drop the る and add the ending: 食べ + ます, 食べ + ない, 食べ + た.

Watch out: a few verbs look like this but are う-verbs: 帰る, 入る, 走る, 知る. Those you just have to learn.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 20

モダン焼やき、できる？

"Can you make modan-yaki?"

できる is the dictionary form of a る-verb: the verb exactly as the dictionary lists it, ending in る. Said like this, it's casual.

On this card, it answers "Is that possible?". As a casual question, you just raise your voice at the end, no か needed.

Polite: drop the る and add ます: できます. Nothing else moves, and that's what makes it a る-verb.

Polite

YouTube · video

これは、すごく共感きょうかんできます。

"I can really relate to this."

Same verb, polite: できる → できます. 共感できる = "can relate".

A verb alone can be a sentence

Japanese doesn't need a subject, so one verb can be the whole sentence. The context tells you who's doing it.

Kekkon Dekinai Otoko · Episode 6

やめる

"[I] quit."

Casual

Demon Slayer - Kimetsu no Yaiba · Episode 6

信しんじる！

"[I] believe [you]!"

Casual

Good Morning Call · Episode 13

食たべる

"[I'll] eat [some]."

Casual

Examples

A friend asks about your Sunday mornings.

日曜にちよう日ひは、昼ひるまで寝ねるよ。

"On Sundays I sleep till noon."

寝る (to sleep). Polite: 寝ます.

Casual

Asking a coworker about lunch.

いつもここで昼ひるご飯はんを食たべますか。

"Do you always eat lunch here?"

食べる → 食べます.

Polite

Your friend asks what you're doing tonight.

今夜こんやは家いえで映画えいがを見みる。

"I'm watching a movie at home tonight."

The dictionary form also works for the future.

Casual

Telling your teacher about your mornings.

毎朝まいあさ六ろく時じに起おきます。

"I get up at six every morning."

起きる → 起きます.

Polite

"Okay. I'll think it over with you."

考える → 考えます: drop る, add ます.

コンピューターの電源でんげんを入いれる。

朝あさは自分じぶんで起おきる。

"I'll wake up on my own in the morning."

Casual

Million Yen Woman · Episode 1

夕食ゆうしょくは 全員ぜんいん一緒いっしょに食たべる。

"Everyone eats dinner together."

Tae Kim's Guide to Japanese Grammar

Verb Basics · Classifying verbs

Polite Form and Verb Stems · Using 「～ます」 to make verbs polite

N5 Grammar

う-Verb (Dictionary)

Polite～ます u sound → i, add ます
Casual～う dictionary form

Same meaning. Only the politeness changes.

Japanese has three types of verbs. This page is about the first one, the う-verbs.

Verb typeDictionaryPolite
1う-verbmost verbs · this page書くalso 飲む, 話す, 買う...書きますu sound → i sound, add ます
2る-verb食べるalso 見る, 起きる, 寝る...食べますdrop る, add ます
3Irregularjust these two verbsする
来る		します
来ますjust learn these
How to tell which type a verb is
  1. Step 1

    Is it する or 来る?

    Yes: Irregular. No: go to step 2.

  2. Step 2

    Does it end in る?

    No: う-verb (書く, 飲む). Yes: go to step 3.

  3. Step 3

    Is the sound just before る an i or an e?

    No: う-verb (分かる wa-ka-ru, 作る tsu-ku-ru).

    Yes: usually a る-verb (見る mi-ru, 食べる ta-be-ru).

A few break step 3. These look like る-verbs but are う-verbs: 帰る, 入る, 走る, 知る.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 13

願ねがいごとが叶かなうよ。

"Your wish will come true."

叶う is the dictionary form: the verb exactly as the dictionary lists it, ending in an u sound (here う). Said like this, it's casual, and it can mean "it happens" or "it will happen".

On this card, he's explaining what happens if you hang a wish on the bamboo, so here it's the future.

Polite: 叶います. The last sound moves from u to i (う → い), then ます goes on. That change is what makes it a う-verb.

Polite

YouTube · video

最近さいきんはあの岐阜ぎふ県けんによく行いきます。

"These days I often go to Gifu."

Same move on another verb: 行く → 行きます. You'd say it to people you don't know well.

Most Japanese verbs are う-verbs, and their dictionary form ends in an u sound.

Every ending

The last sound moves from the u row to the i row, then ます.

Dictionary→ます
買かう→買かいますbuy
書かく→書かきますwrite
急いそぐ→急いそぎますhurry
貸かす→貸かしますlend
待まつ→待まちますwait
死しぬ→死しにますdie
遊あそぶ→遊あそびますplay
読よむ→読よみますread

Only this row is confusing. Every ending above is always a う-verb. A verb ending in る can be a う-verb or a る-verb.

作つくる→作つくりますmake

Careful with る. Look at the sound right before it. With an a, u or o sound, it's always a う-verb: 作る → 作ります. With an i or e sound, it's usually a る-verb, where る just drops: 食べる → 食べます. A few common verbs break that and are う-verbs anyway: 帰る → 帰ります.

In Japanese, う-verbs are called 五段 (godan), "five steps".

A verb alone can be a sentence

Japanese doesn't need a subject, so one verb can be the whole sentence. The context tells you who's doing it.

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 3

違ちがう。

"[That's] not it."

Casual

Samurai Champloo · Episode 13

断ことわる

"[I] refuse."

Casual

Good Morning Call · Episode 12

頼たのむ

"[I'm] begging [you]."

Casual

Examples

Your friend asks if you're getting the new game.

うん、買かう！

"Yeah, I'll buy it!"

To a coworker: 買います.

Casual

The barista asks if your coffee is to go.

ここで飲のみます。

"I'll drink it here."

飲む → 飲みます: む becomes み.

Polite

Your friend texts: "running 10 minutes late, sorry!"

じゃあ、カフェで待まつ。

"Okay, I'll wait at the café."

Polite: 待ちます. つ becomes ち.

Casual

A client asks when you'll send the finished drawings.

明日あした送おくります。

"I'll send them tomorrow."

送る → 送ります: る becomes り.

Polite

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

この質問しつもんをたくさんもらいます。

"I get this question a lot."

もらう → もらいます: う becomes い.

Polite

YouTube · Japanese Listening Practice With A Story #10

じゃあ、２０分ぷんぐらい煮込にこみます。

"Okay, now we simmer it for about 20 minutes."

煮込む → 煮込みます. Recipes and how-tos love the ます form.

Polite

YouTube · My Five Favorite Things

僕ぼくは毎朝まいあさ、この髭剃ひげそりを使つかいます。

"I use this razor every morning."

使う → 使います: う becomes い.

Casual

Last Samurai Standing · Episode 1

十也、手拭てぬぐいを頼たのむ。

"Toya, get me a hand towel."

頼む is "to ask for". The dictionary form makes it a short, casual request. Polite: 頼みます.

Casual

PiroPito · First Playthrough of Minecraft #06

家いえの中なかに逃にげ込こむ。

"[I'll] run into the house."

Talking to himself while playing, so casual. 逃げ込む is "to run in to hide". Polite: 逃げ込みます.

Casual

Pokémon: Indigo League · Episode 1

木きの実みなどの硬かたい物ものやチーズを好このむ。

"Likes hard things like nuts and cheese."

The Pokédex talks like a written description, and those use the dictionary form. 好む → 好みます.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 5

今日きょうはもう帰かえるね。

"I'm heading home now for today."

Polite would be 帰ります.

N5 Grammar

る-Verb (Negative)

Polite～ません drop る, add ません
Casual～ない drop る, add ない

Same meaning: "don't, doesn't". Only the politeness changes.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 2

少すこし塩気しおけが足たりないね

"[It] needs a little more salt."

To say a る-verb is not happening, drop the る and add ない: 足りる (to be enough) → 足りない (isn't enough).

On this card, he's tasting the food. The sentence answers "Is there enough salt?": no, it's a little short. The ね at the end is just "huh", sharing the thought.

Polite: drop the る and add ません: 足りません.

Polite

YouTube · video

あれ？！思おもったほど散歩さんぽしている人ひとがいません。

"Huh?! There aren't as many people out walking as I thought."

Same move, polite: いる (to be there, for people and animals) → いません. Casual would be いない.

Examples

A friend holds out a pack of natto for you.

納豆なっとうは食たべない。

"I don't eat natto."

To a coworker: 食べません.

Casual

A coworker asks if you saw the match last night.

サッカーはあまり見みません。

"I don't really watch soccer."

見る → 見ません. Just the る goes.

Polite

Your friend asks if you want to go out tonight. It's raining.

今日きょうは出でかけない。

"I'm not going out today."

ない works for "don't" and "won't". There's no separate future.

Casual

Your host family drops you at the airport on your last day.

この夏なつは忘わすれません。

"I won't forget this summer."

Polite

With and without

Plain

肉にくを食たべる。

"I eat meat."

With ない

肉にくを食たべない。

"I don't eat meat." る out, ない in.

Polite

肉にくを食たべません。

Same meaning. る out, ません in.

Not this

肉にくを食たべらない。

That's the う-verb move (帰る → 帰らない). る-verbs just drop the る.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

もうすぐ朝あさ６時じですけど、意外いがいと散歩さんぽしている人ひとがあんまりいないですね。

"It's almost 6 a.m., but surprisingly there aren't many people out walking."

いない + です is another polite way, a little softer than いません. Same guy, same walk as the card above.

Polite

Quartet · Episode 2

アイス食たべないんですか？

"You're not having any ice cream?"

食べない + んですか: asking why not.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 15

食たべないの　パンダ　あんぱん

"Aren't you eating [your] anpan, Panda?"

食べる → 食べない. The の after it makes it a question that asks for the story: why aren't you eating it?

Casual

New Atashin'chi · Episode 2

あたしって２つのことが同時どうじにできないんだよね。

"I just can't do two things at once."

できる (can do) is a る-verb, so できない. The んだよね after it is her explaining herself.

Casual

Weakest Beast · Episode 9

世間せけんは そう見みないから。

"Because people won't see it that way."

見る ("see") → 見ない = "won't see". 世間 ("people, society") + は + そう ("that way"). から: "because".

Casual

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 2

もう食たべないの？

"You're done eating?"

もう ("anymore") + 食べない ("not eating") = "not eating anymore?". の makes it a soft question.

Casual

Erased · Episode 9

俺おれが信しんじるか信しんじないかだ。

"It's about whether I believe it or not."

信じる ("believe") → 信じない. 信じるか信じないか = "whether I believe it or not".

Negative Verbs · Conjugating verbs into the negative

Polite Form and Verb Stems · Using 「～ます」 to make verbs polite

N5 Grammar

う-Verb (Negative)

Polite～ません u sound → i, add ません
Casual～ない u sound → a, add ない

Same meaning: "don't, doesn't". Only the politeness changes.

Polite

YouTube · video

ただこれは神かみ様さまのお話はなしなので、本当ほんとうかどうかは分わかりません。

"But this is a story about the gods, so we don't know if it's true."

To say a う-verb is not happening, politely: move the last sound from u to i, then add ません. 分かる (to know) → 分かりません. Same i sound as before ます.

On this card, the speaker is telling an old legend. The sentence answers "Is it true?": nobody knows.

Casual: move the last sound from u to a, then add ない: 分からない.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 4

いや、寝ねてても構かまわないけど

"Nah, I don't mind if you sleep, though."

Same move, casual: 構う (to mind) → 構わない. It ends in う, so it goes to わ, not あ.

Examples

A friend asks where Tanaka went.

知しらない。

"No idea."

知る → 知らない. る moves to ら, then ない.

Casual

A coworker asks if you're coming for drinks after work.

今日きょうは飲のみません。

"I'm not drinking today."

飲む → 飲みません. む moves to み, same as 飲みます.

Polite

You're in a shop with a friend. They hold up a jacket that costs way too much.

高たかいから買かわない。

"It's too expensive, so I'm not buying it."

One catch: verbs ending in う go to わ, not あ. 買う → 買わない.

Casual

You and a coworker look out the window. It's been raining all day.

雨あめがなかなか止やみません。

"The rain just won't stop."

ません works for "don't" and "won't". There's no separate future.

Polite

With and without

Plain

コーヒーを飲のむ。

"I drink coffee."

With ない

コーヒーを飲のまない。

"I don't drink coffee." む → ま, then ない.

Polite

コーヒーを飲のみません。

Same meaning. む → み, then ません.

Not this

コーヒーを飲のむない。

ない never goes straight on the dictionary form. The last sound has to change first.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

でも多分たぶんそれではうまくいかないんですね

"But that probably won't work, huh."

いく → いかない. うまくいかない = "doesn't go well". The んですね after it makes the whole thing polite.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 20

う～ん…　ベロが届とどかないよ！

"Ugh... my tongue can't reach!"

届く → 届かない: the く sound becomes か, then ない.

Casual

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 11

もう何なにも言いわない。

"I won't say anything anymore."

言う ("say") → 言わない: う becomes わ. もう何も: "nothing anymore".

Casual

Weakest Beast · Episode 9

全まったく分わからない。

"I have no idea."

分かる ("understand") → 分からない: る becomes ら. 全く: "at all".

Casual

Fermat Kitchen · Episode 7

宍戸ししど君くん、行いかないの？

"Shishido, aren't you going?"

行く ("go") → 行かない: く becomes か. の makes it a question: "aren't you going?".

Casual

Code Geass · Episode 8

一緒いっしょに行いかない？

"Want to come with us?"

行く ("go") → 行かない with a rising voice: "won't you go?", a friendly invitation. 一緒に: "together".

Casual

Border · Episode 7

まだ 分わからない

"I don't know yet."

分かる → 分からない.

Polite Form and Verb Stems · Using 「～ます」 to make verbs polite

N5 Grammar

る-Verb (Past)

Polite～ました drop る, add ました
Casual～た drop る, add た

Same meaning: "did". Only the politeness changes.

Casual

YouTube · video

あ、できた。

"Oh, [I] did it."

To say a る-verb already happened, drop the る and add た: できる (can do, to get done) → できた (got done).

On this card, the sentence answers "Did it work?": yes, it's done. One word is enough, the "I" and the "it" are clear from the scene.

Polite: drop the る and add ました: できました.

Polite

YouTube · Let's learn Japanese while walking to Asakusa!!

僕ぼくもさっき、抹茶まっちゃのスイーツを食たべました。

"I had a matcha sweet a moment ago too."

Same move, polite: 食べる → 食べました. Casual would be 食べた.

Examples

A friend asks if you want to grab something to eat.

もう食たべた。

"I already ate."

To a coworker: 食べました.

Casual

A coworker asks what you did on the weekend.

映画えいがを見みました。

"I watched a movie."

見る → 見ました. Just the る goes.

Polite

A friend asks why you look so tired.

昨日きのうは三さん時じに寝ねた。

"I went to bed at three last night."

寝る → 寝た.

Casual

The teacher asks for your homework. It's still on your desk at home.

すみません、忘わすれました。

"Sorry, I forgot."

Polite

With and without

Plain

朝あさごはんを食たべる。

"I eat breakfast." (or "I'll eat")

With た

朝あさごはんを食たべた。

"I ate breakfast." る out, た in.

Polite

朝あさごはんを食たべました。

Same meaning. る out, ました in.

Not this

朝あさごはんを食たべった。

That's the う-verb move (帰る → 帰った). る-verbs just drop the る.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

カレールウを入いれましたか？

"Did you put in the curry roux?"

入れる (to put in) → 入れました. The か turns it into a question.

Polite

YouTube · video

はい、皆みなさん、えっと、今いま私わたしたちも浴衣ゆかたに着替きがえましたよ。

"Okay everyone, um, we've changed into yukata now too."

着替える (to change clothes) → 着替えました. The よ tells you something new.

Casual

YouTube · video

なんか動画どうが見みた気きがする。

"I feel like I saw a video [about it]."

見る → 見た. 気がする after it is "I feel like". The を after 動画 is dropped, normal in casual talk.

Casual

YouTube · video

友達ともだちが海外かいがいに1ヶ月いっかげつ旅たびに出でた、だから、その間あいだに使つかっていいよ。

"My friend went on a trip abroad for a month, so you can use it in the meantime."

出る (to leave, to set out) → 出た. 旅に出る is "to set off on a trip".

Casual

Source unknown No source

キャベツの中なかに、毛虫けむしがいた。

"There was a caterpillar in the cabbage."

いる → いた. Polite: いました.

Casual

Source unknown No source

それでも、人ひとはたくさんいたけどね。

"Still, there were lots of people, though."

いる → いた. けどね at the end softens it: "though, huh".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 40

あぁ、よく寝ねた。

"Ah, I slept well."

寝る drops る, adds た.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 24

決きめたよ！

"I've decided!"

決める drops る, adds た.

Past Tense · Past tense for ru-verbs

Polite Form and Verb Stems · Using 「～ます」 to make verbs polite

N5 Grammar

う-Verb (Past)

Ends inVerbPoliteCasual
う つ る買う買いました買った
く書く書きました書いた
ぐ急ぐ急ぎました急いだ
ぬ ぶ む飲む飲みました飲んだ
す出す出しました出した
odd one行く行きました行った

Same meaning: "did". Polite is always the same: the last sound moves to i, then ました. Casual depends on the last sound.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 3

だから言いったのに

"I told you so."

To say a う-verb already happened, casually: the last sound changes, then comes た. Which change depends on that last sound. 言う (to say) ends in う, so it becomes 言った. Verbs ending in う, つ or る all go to った.

On this card, something went wrong and the speaker had warned about it. The sentence answers "Did you say anything?": yes, I said it, and still...

Polite: same move as before ます, u → i, then ました: 言いました. No sound changes there.

Polite

Quartet · Episode 1

バディソープ買かいましたよ

"I bought body soap."

The polite past is the same for every う-verb: swap ます for ました, with no sound changes. On this card, 買います → 買いました.

Examples

A friend offers you a coffee. You just had one.

もう飲のんだ。

"I already had one."

飲む → 飲んだ. Verbs ending in む, ぶ or ぬ go to んだ.

Casual

A coworker asks what you did on the weekend.

京都きょうとに行いきました。

"I went to Kyoto."

行く → 行きました. u → i, then ました.

Polite

A friend asks if you messaged the teacher about tomorrow.

うん、昨日きのう書かいた。

"Yeah, I wrote [to them] yesterday."

書く → 書いた. く goes to いた, ぐ goes to いだ (泳ぐ → 泳いだ).

Casual

Your friend shows up late and asks how long you waited.

三十分さんじゅっぷん待まちましたよ。

"I waited thirty minutes, you know."

待つ → 待ちました. Casual: 待った (つ goes to った).

Polite

With and without

Plain

手紙てがみを書かく。

"I write a letter." (or "I'll write")

With た

手紙てがみを書かいた。

"I wrote a letter." く changes to い, then た.

Polite

手紙てがみを書かきました。

Same meaning. く → き, then ました.

Not this

学校がっこうに行おこないた。

行く is the one odd verb: it ends in く but goes to 行った, not 行いた.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

河口かわぐち湖このエリアに着つきましたよ。

"We've arrived in the Lake Kawaguchi area."

着く (to arrive) → 着きました. The よ tells you something new.

Polite

YouTube · video

そう、車検しゃけんをするために地元じもとに帰かえりました。

"Right, I went back to my hometown for the car inspection."

帰る (to go home) → 帰りました. It looks like a る-verb but it's a う-verb, so the る becomes り.

Polite

YouTube · video

昔むかしはえーと日本にほんに蒸気じょうき機関きかん車しゃがたくさんありましたね。

"Back then, um, there were lots of steam trains in Japan."

ある (to be there, for things) → ありました. Casual: あった.

Casual

New Atashin'chi · Episode 1

分わかったからシーッ！

"Okay, I get it, so shh!"

分かる (to understand) → 分かった. It ends in る, so った.

Casual

YouTube · video

子こどもの頃ころ、僕ぼくが山やまで遊あそんだ時とき、毎日まいにち冒険ぼうけんみたいな感かんじでした。

"When I played in the mountains as a kid, every day felt like an adventure."

遊ぶ (to play) → 遊んだ. ぶ goes to んだ. Before 時 (when) the casual form stays, even in a polite sentence.

Casual

Source unknown No source

先週せんしゅう、彼かれと会議かいぎ室しつで話はなした。

"I talked with him in the meeting room last week."

話す (to talk) → 話した. す goes to した.

Casual

Source unknown No source

机つくえの上うえに虫むし眼鏡めがねを置おいた。

"I put the magnifying glass on the desk."

置く (to put) → 置いた. く goes to いた.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 38

海うみにも行おこなったね。

"We went to the sea too."

行く is the odd one: 行った.

Reference

A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

Appendix 1, Basic Conjugations (Group 1 verbs) · pp. 576–577

Polite Form and Verb Stems · Using 「～ます」 to make verbs polite

N5 Grammar

Verb (Past negative)

Polite～ませんでした standard polite
～なかったです everyday, softer
Casual～なかった

Same meaning: "didn't". Only the politeness changes.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 12

常勤じょうきんパンダさんが、モデラーなんて知しらなかったよ。

"I didn't know Full-Time Panda built models."

なかった means didn't: the negative, in the past. Take the ない form and swap ない for なかった: 知らない → 知らなかった.

On this card, it answers "Did you know?": no, not until now. It works the same for every verb: 食べない → 食べなかった, しない → しなかった, 来ない → 来なかった.

Polite: swap ます for ませんでした: 知ります → 知りませんでした.

Polite

NHK News Web Easy · article

前半ぜんはんは、日本にほんもオランダも点てんが取とれませんでした。

"In the first half, neither Japan nor the Netherlands scored."

Polite: 取れます → 取れませんでした. 取れる = "can get", so literally "couldn't get a point".

Examples

A friend asks how the party was.

昨日きのう、パーティーに行いかなかった。

"I didn't go to the party yesterday."

行かない → 行かなかった.

Casual

Your teacher asks for your homework.

すみません、宿題しゅくだいをしませんでした。

"Sorry, I didn't do my homework."

します → しませんでした.

Polite

A coworker offers you a snack.

今朝けさは何なにも食たべませんでした。

"I didn't eat anything this morning."

何も + negative = nothing.

Polite

A friend asks if you saw their message.

ごめん、見みなかった。

"Sorry, I didn't see it."

見ない → 見なかった.

Casual

With and without

Without

パーティーに行いかない。

"I'm not going to the party." Now or later.

With なかった

パーティーに行いかなかった。

"I didn't go to the party." It's over, and I wasn't there.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

胃いもたれしなかったです。

"My stomach didn't feel heavy."

なかった + です: polite, a bit softer than ませんでした.

Polite

YouTube · video

そういう、簡単かんたんなフレーズさえ話はなせませんでした。

"I couldn't even say simple phrases like that."

話せる (can speak) → 話せませんでした.

Polite

YouTube · video

ネットに繋つながらなくて、開あけませんでした。

"It wasn't online, so I couldn't open it."

開けます → 開けませんでした.

Polite

Source unknown No source

階段かいだんの上うえには、誰だれもいませんでした。

"There was nobody at the top of the stairs."

いる → いませんでした. 誰も + negative = nobody.

Casual

Source unknown No source

あれ？ウケなかった？

"Huh? That didn't get a laugh?"

ウケる (to get a laugh) → ウケなかった.

Casual

Source unknown No source

昨夜さくやは、悪夢あくむを見みてよく眠ねむれなかった。

"I had a nightmare last night and couldn't sleep well."

眠れる (can sleep) → 眠れなかった.

Casual

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 4

知しらなかった。

"I had no idea."

知る ("know") → 知らない → 知らなかった = "didn't know", "I had no idea".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 19

へぇ～、知しらなかった。

"Huh, I didn't know that."

知らない becomes 知らなかった.

Polite Form and Verb Stems · Using 「～ます」 to make verbs polite

N5 Grammar

来る

Polite来ます (きます)
Casual来る (くる)

Same meaning: "to come". Only the politeness changes.

Japanese has three types of verbs. This page is about the third one, the irregular verbs: 来る.

Verb typeDictionaryPolite
1う-verbmost verbs書くalso 飲む, 話す, 買う...書きますu sound → i sound, add ます
2る-verb食べるalso 見る, 起きる, 寝る...食べますdrop る, add ます
3Irregularjust these two verbs · this pageする
来る		します
来ますjust learn these
How to tell which type a verb is
  1. Step 1

    Is it する or 来る?

    Yes: Irregular. No: go to step 2.

  2. Step 2

    Does it end in る?

    No: う-verb (書く, 飲む). Yes: go to step 3.

  3. Step 3

    Is the sound just before る an i or an e?

    No: う-verb (分かる wa-ka-ru, 作る tsu-ku-ru).

    Yes: usually a る-verb (見る mi-ru, 食べる ta-be-ru).

A few break step 3. These look like る-verbs but are う-verbs: 帰る, 入る, 走る, 知る.

Casual

YouTube · video

ここには、ゴンドラで来くることもできる。

"You can also come here by gondola."

来る (くる) means to come: to move toward the place where the speaker is, or will be. It's an irregular verb, so the kanji stays the same but the reading changes (くる, き, こ).

On this card, the sentence answers "How can you get here?": by gondola. 来る is the casual dictionary form, and it sits right before こと.

Polite

YouTube · video

はい、今いま、注文ちゅうもんした五平餅もちが来きました！見みえますか？

"Okay, the gohei-mochi I ordered just arrived! Can you see it?"

Polite past: 来る → 来ました (きました). The food came to the table where he is, so 来る is "arrived". Casual would be 来た (きた).

Examples

You're on the phone with a friend. Your dinner plans are tonight.

今夜こんや、うちに来くる？

"Are you coming to my place tonight?"

Just 来る with a rising voice, no か needed.

Casual

You're the manager. A new hire is starting tomorrow.

明日あしたは何なん時じに来きますか。

"What time will you come tomorrow?"

来る → 来ます. Say it きます.

Polite

A friend asks if Ken is joining the barbecue.

ケンは今日きょうは来こないよ。

"Ken isn't coming today."

Not 来らない. The く turns into こ: こない. Polite: 来ません (きません).

Casual

Your friend asks who showed up at the office this morning.

社長しゃちょうが朝あさ早はやく来きました。

"The boss came in early this morning."

Polite

Your mom calls you down: dinner is ready.

今いま、行いく！

"I'm coming!"

English says "coming", Japanese says "going" (行く) when you head to where the other person is. 来る is for coming to where you are, or will be.

Casual

With and without

Casual

友達ともだちが来くる。

"A friend comes." Reading: くる.

Not coming

友達ともだちが来こない。

"A friend doesn't come." Reading: こない.

Polite

友達ともだちが来きます。

Same as 来る, polite. Reading: きます.

Not this

友達ともだちが来こらない。

That's the う-verb move (帰る → 帰らない). 来る is irregular: く becomes こ.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

さっきの方々かたがたは、ツアーで来きてますね。

"The people from earlier are here for a tour."

来て + います (said as 来てます). They came and they're still here, so English says "are here".

Polite

From Up on Poppy Hill

お寿司すしが来きましたよ！

"The sushi's here!"

来ました (きました): polite past.

Polite

Border · Episode 3

今こん 刑事けいじが来きました

"A detective just came."

来る → 来ました: polite past.

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 4

また来きます。

"I'll come again."

来ます reads きます.

Casual

The Journalist · Episode 2

また来くるよ。

"I'll come again."

また ("again") + 来る (くる) = "I'll come again". The dictionary form covers "will".

Casual

Weakest Beast · Episode 5

誰だれか来きたの？

"Did someone come?"

誰か ("someone") + 来た (きた, "came") = "did someone come?". の makes it a soft question.

Casual

Legal High · Episode 1

何なにしに来きた！

"What are you here for?!"

何しに ("to do what") + 来た ("came") = "what did you come here for?!". Rough and angry.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 50

あっ、来きた。

"Oh, here he comes."

来た reads きた.

Tae Kim's Guide to Japanese Grammar

Verb Basics · Classifying verbs

N5 Grammar

する

Politeします
Casualする

Same meaning: "to do". Only the politeness changes.

Japanese has three types of verbs. This page is about the third one, the irregular verbs: する.

Verb typeDictionaryPolite
1う-verbmost verbs書くalso 飲む, 話す, 買う...書きますu sound → i sound, add ます
2る-verb食べるalso 見る, 起きる, 寝る...食べますdrop る, add ます
3Irregularjust these two verbs · this pageする
来る		します
来ますjust learn these
How to tell which type a verb is
  1. Step 1

    Is it する or 来る?

    Yes: Irregular. No: go to step 2.

  2. Step 2

    Does it end in る?

    No: う-verb (書く, 飲む). Yes: go to step 3.

  3. Step 3

    Is the sound just before る an i or an e?

    No: う-verb (分かる wa-ka-ru, 作る tsu-ku-ru).

    Yes: usually a る-verb (見る mi-ru, 食べる ta-be-ru).

A few break step 3. These look like る-verbs but are う-verbs: 帰る, 入る, 走る, 知る.

Polite

YouTube · video

皆みなさんは、１日いちにちの終おわりに何なにをしますか？

"What do you all do at the end of the day?"

する means to do. The thing you do comes before it with を (何をする, テニスをする), or an action noun sits right in front of it (勉強する, 料理する).

It's an irregular verb: in most forms the す turns into し (します, しない, した). On this card, the sentence asks "What activity?": 何をしますか.

Casual

Pokémon The Series: Indigo League · Episode 2

悪役あくやくさん、わたしが相手あいてをするわ。

"Hey, villain, I'll take you on."

Casual dictionary form する, here for something she's about to do. 相手をする is "be someone's opponent". The わ at the end just softens it.

Examples

You're texting a friend on Friday night.

週末しゅうまつ、何なにする？

"What are you doing this weekend?"

In casual speech the を often drops out: 何をする → 何する.

Casual

A coworker asks what you do in the evenings.

毎晩まいばん、日本にほん語ごの勉強べんきょうをします。

"I study Japanese every evening."

勉強をします and 勉強します mean the same thing.

Polite

Your roommate asks if you're cleaning today. You're tired.

今日きょうは掃除そうじしない。

"I'm not cleaning today."

Not すらない. The す turns into し: しない. Polite: しません.

Casual

Your teacher asks what you did yesterday.

友達ともだちとテニスをしました。

"I played tennis with a friend."

English says "play", Japanese just says "do" for sports and games.

Polite

Your friend lent you a new game last week.

あのゲーム、もうした？

"Did you play that game yet?"

Casual past: する → した. Polite: しました.

Casual

With and without

Casual

宿題しゅくだいをする。

"I do homework."

Not doing

宿題しゅくだいをしない。

"I don't do homework."

Polite

宿題しゅくだいをします。

Same as する, polite.

Not this

宿題しゅくだいをすらない。

That's the う-verb move (帰る → 帰らない). する is irregular: す becomes し.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

見みて、私わたしはつけ麺めんを注文ちゅうもんしましたよ。

"Look, I ordered tsukemen."

注文 (an order) + する = to order. Polite past: しました.

Polite

YouTube · video

最近さいきん、いつも僕ぼくは朝あさ早はやい時間じかん、赤あかちゃんのお世話せわをします。

"These days I always look after the baby early in the morning."

お世話をする = to take care of. します for something he does every day.

Polite

I am Mita, Your Housekeeper · Episode 2

失礼しつれいします。

"Excuse me."

失礼 ("rudeness") + します = "excuse me". Said when you walk into or out of a room.

Polite

Sailor Suit and Machine Gun · Episode 1

しません。

"We won't."

する ("do") → しません = "we won't do it". A flat, polite refusal.

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 1

発表はっぴょうします。

"I'll announce it."

Noun + します.

Casual

Quartet · Episode 7

したよ…

"I did."

する ("do") → した = "I did". よ: telling them, a bit defensive.

Casual

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 5

何なにする？

"What should we have?"

何 ("what") + する ("do") = "what'll we do?", here "what should we order?". を dropped, casual.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 46

そうするよ。

"I'll do that."

そうする = do it that way.

Reference

A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

Entry "suru¹" (do) · pp. 428–433

Tae Kim's Guide to Japanese Grammar

Verb Basics · Classifying verbs

N5 Grammar

Verb + Noun

Verb + Noun

A verb right before a noun describes that noun. Nothing goes in between: no の, no な.

買った本 = "the book I bought"
飲んでいる人 = "the person drinking"
住んでいるところ = "the place where I live"

Casual

YouTube · video

今いま住すんでいるところは千葉ちば県けん。

"Where I live now is Chiba."

On this card, 住んでいる (live) + ところ (place) = the place where I live. It answers "Which place?": the one I live in now.

In polite speech it's still 住んでいるところです, never ます before the noun. Only the end of the sentence shows the politeness.

Polite

YouTube · video

2025年ねんに、大だいヒットした映画えいががあります。

"There's a movie that was a huge hit in 2025."

Past works too: 大ヒットした (was a big hit) + 映画 = a movie that was a big hit. Polite only because of あります at the end.

Examples

At a party, pointing at someone.

あそこでビールを飲のんでいる人ひとは誰だれ？

"Who's that guy drinking beer over there?"

Everything before 人 describes the person.

Casual

Telling a coworker about a book.

昨日きのう買かった本ほんはとても面白おもしろいです。

"The book I bought yesterday is really good."

買った (bought) + 本 = the book I bought.

Polite

Looking at a menu with a friend.

食たべたいもの、ある？

"Anything you want to eat?"

たい works too: 食べたい + もの = a thing I want to eat.

Casual

Asking a station worker.

新宿しんじゅくに行いく電車でんしゃはどれですか。

"Which train goes to Shinjuku?"

行く + 電車 = the train that goes.

Polite

With and without

Without

これは本ほんです。

"This is a book." Just some book.

With Verb + Noun

これは昨日きのう買かった本ほんです。

"This is the book I bought yesterday." The verb tells you which book.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

卵たまごアレルギーの人ひとでも食たべられるもの、ありますか？

"Is there anything people with an egg allergy can eat?"

食べられる (can eat) + もの = things you can eat.

Polite

Source unknown No source

このへんに、キャンプに来くる人ひとも多おおいです。

"Lots of people come camping around here too."

来る + 人 = people who come.

Polite

Source unknown No source

１回かい揚あげたものを、もう一いち度ど揚あげます。

"Take what you fried once and fry it again."

揚げた (fried) + もの = the thing you fried.

Casual

YouTube · video

こんな感かんじで、電化でんか製せい品ひんとかを売うっている場所ばしょが多おおいね。

"There are lots of places like this that sell electronics."

売っている (are selling) + 場所 = places that sell.

Casual

YouTube · video

あ、夜よる、夜よる食たべる人ひとはもうサクっと食たべて。

"Oh, if you're having it at night, just eat it quick."

食べる + 人 = people who eat.

Casual

Pokémon The Series: Indigo League · Episode 1

あのね、ピカチュウ、この状態じょうたいずーっと続つづける気き？

"Hey, Pikachu, you plan to keep this up forever?"

続ける (to keep going) + 気 (intention) = the plan to keep going.

Casual

YouTube · video

春はるになると、桜さくらアンマン、しかも、中なかにお餅もちが入はいっているもの。

"In spring there are sakura buns, and even ones with mochi inside."

入っている (is inside) + もの = ones that have it inside.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 46

じゃあ、何なにか食たべるもの作つくるね。

"Then I'll make something to eat."

食べる describes もの: things to eat.

Reference

A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

Entry "Relative Clause" · pp. 376–380

Tae Kim's Guide to Japanese Grammar

Relative Clauses and Sentence Order · Using relative verb clauses as adjectives

N5 Grammar

が → の

Why swap が for の?

So the sentence doesn't have two が. With の, the label on the noun is easy to spot, and the one real が stays for the main sentence:

母が作ったケーキが好き = two が, clunky
母の作ったケーキが好き = smoother, you'll hear this one

You never have to swap: が is always correct. Just know that の + verb or adjective means が, not "my".

Polite

Only Yesterday

意見いけんのある人ひとは 手てをあげてください！

"Anyone who has an opinion, raise your hand!"

When a verb or adjective describes a noun (作った + ケーキ, "the cake I made"), the が in front of it can become の: 私が作ったケーキ = 私の作ったケーキ. Same meaning. This only happens in that describing part; in a normal sentence it stays が (私がケーキを作った). On this card, at a class meeting, the chair calls on anyone with an opinion: 意見のある + 人, the same as 意見がある人.

Casual

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 11

だってここが、私わたしのいる場所ばしょだから。

"Because this is where I belong."

On this card, Aya says why she wants to stay: 私のいる + 場所, "the place where I am", the same as 私がいる場所.

Examples

A coworker asks about your favorite food.

母ははの作つくったカレーが一番いちばん好すきです。

"I like the curry my mom makes best."

母の作った + カレー = "the curry my mom made".

Polite

Showing a guest a picture on the wall.

これは父ちちの撮とった写真しゃしんです。

"This is a photo my dad took."

Polite

Telling a friend about your weekend.

友達ともだちの住すんでる町まちに行いったよ。

"I went to the town where my friend lives."

Casual

Karaoke night. You hand your friend the mic.

君きみの好すきな歌うた、歌うたってよ。

"Sing a song you like."

Works with adjectives too: 君の好きな + 歌.

Casual

With and without

With が

私わたしが作つくったケーキです。

"It's the cake I made." Correct, a bit plain.

With の

私わたしの作つくったケーキです。

"It's the cake I made." Same meaning, smoother. You'll hear this one a lot.

Sentence mining

Polite

Source unknown No source

僕ぼくの育そだった町まち、僕ぼくのふるさとは山形やまがた県けんです。

"The town where I grew up, my hometown, is in Yamagata."

僕の育った + 町 = "the town I grew up in".

Polite

Quartet · Episode 8

私わたしの好すきな人ひとに あげてもいいですか？

"Can I give this to the person I like?"

私の好きな + 人 = "the person I like".

Polite

Death Note · Episode 13

ほら、僕ぼくの言いったとおりでしょう？

"See? It's just like I said."

僕の言った + とおり ("the way") = "the way I said".

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 41

いちじくのある家いえですよ。

"It's the house with the fig tree."

Before a noun, が can become の: いちじくがある家.

Casual

I am Mita, Your Housekeeper · Episode 9

もう三田みたさんの作つくった料理りょうり 食たべれないのか

"So we can't eat Mita's cooking anymore?"

三田さんの作った + 料理 = "the food Mita made".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 2

僕ぼくの好すきなものは　皆みなもきっと好すきだよ

"Everyone's sure to like the things I like."

僕の好きな + もの = "the things I like".

Casual

Howl's Moving Castle

もうすぐよ　私わたしの生うまれた町まちだわ。

"We're almost there. It's the town where I was born."

私の生まれた + 町 = "the town I was born in".

Casual

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 3

あなたの好すきなウニあるわよ

"There's the sea urchin you like."

あなたの好きな + ウニ = "the sea urchin you like".

Reference

A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

Entry "Relative Clause", Note 3 · p. 378

N5 Grammar

～にする

Polite～にします
Casual～にする

Same meaning: "I'll go with ___". Only the politeness changes.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 19

うん、コーヒー、今日きょうは、ブラックにする。

"Yeah, coffee. Today I'll have it black."

Noun + にする means decide on, go with: you pick one thing out of a few choices. It's what you say when ordering or choosing a day, a plan, a color.

On this card, a regular orders coffee and picks how to have it today: ブラックにする, "I'll go with black".

In the past, にした, it means the choice is already made: 理系にした, "I went with science".

Polite

Weakest Beast · Episode 3

これにします

"I'll go with this one."

にします is the polite ～にする: you've made your choice. On this card, これ + にします is what you'd say when picking something in a shop.

Examples

At a café counter. The staff waits for your order.

私わたしはアイスコーヒーにします。

"I'll have an iced coffee."

Polite

The team is trying to pick a day for the meeting.

会議かいぎは金曜きんよう日ひにしましょう。

"Let's make the meeting Friday."

にしましょう: "let's go with ___".

Polite

Looking at the menu in a ramen shop with a friend.

A: 何なににする？
B: 俺おれは味噌みそラーメンにする。

A: "What are you getting?" B: "I'll go with miso ramen."

Casual

You couldn't decide between two jackets. A friend asks which one you bought.

やっぱり、黒くろい方ほうにした。

"In the end, I went with the black one."

にした: the choice is already made.

Casual

With and without

Without

コーヒーを飲のみます。

"I'll drink coffee." Just what you'll do.

With にする

コーヒーにします。

"I'll have coffee." You picked it out of the choices.

N5 Grammar

～たことがある

Polite～たことがあります never: ～たことがありません, ～たことないです
Casual～たことがある・～たことある never: ～たことがない, ～たことない

Same meaning: "have done before". Only the politeness changes.

Take a verb in its た-form and add ことがある: 行った + ことがある = "I've been there before". It's about experience: something that happened at least once in your life, not what you did yesterday.

Never done it: ～たことがない. In speech the が often drops: 行ったことある, 行ったことない.

Polite

YouTube · video

この建物たてものも来きたことがあります。

"I've been to this building too."

ことがあります is the polite ことがある. On this card, 来た + ことがあります = "I've come here before", at least once in his life.

Casual

Million Yen Woman · Episode 6

聞きいたことないな

"Never heard of it."

Never done it is ～たことない, and the が often drops in speech. On this card, 聞いた + ことない = "have never heard", and な is thinking aloud.

Examples

A new coworker asks about your travels.

A: 京都きょうとに行いったことがありますか。
B: はい、一いち度どあります。

A: "Have you ever been to Kyoto?" B: "Yes, once."

The answer can just be あります: the rest is clear.

Polite

Someone offers you natto at breakfast.

納豆なっとうは食たべたことがありません。

"I've never eaten natto."

Polite

Picking a movie with a friend.

この映画えいが、見みたことある？

"Have you ever seen this movie?"

Casual

A friend suggests climbing Mt Fuji this summer.

富士ふじ山やま、まだ登のぼったことないんだ。

"I've never climbed Fuji."

Casual

With and without

Without

京都きょうとに行いきました。

"I went to Kyoto." One trip, at some point.

With ことがある

京都きょうとに行いったことがあります。

"I've been to Kyoto." It's part of your experience.

N5 Grammar

～た方がいい・～ない方がいい

Polite～た方がいいです shouldn't: ～ない方がいいです
Casual～た方がいい shouldn't: ～ない方がいい

Same meaning: "you should, you shouldn't". Only the politeness changes.

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Season 1, Episode 4

読よまれたくないなら、非ひ公開こうかいにした方ほうがいいですよ。

"If you don't want people reading it, you should make it private."

～た方がいい gives advice: you should, it's better to. Put the verb in its た-form, then 方がいい (方 is read ほう): した + 方がいい. For "you shouldn't", use the ない-form: しない方がいい.

On this card, someone is worried people will read their blog, and gets a simple tip: make it private (非公開).

Casual

Good Morning Call · Season 2, Episode 8

早はやくしたほうがいいよ

"You should do it soon."

Without です it's casual, and ほう is often written in kana. On this card, した + ほうがいい = "you should do it", and よ gives it a little push.

Examples

A coworker is sneezing at their desk.

今日きょうは早はやく寝ねた方ほうがいいですよ。

"You should go to bed early tonight."

Polite

A guest reaches for the tap water at an old mountain hut.

その水みずは飲のまない方ほうがいいです。

"You'd better not drink that water."

Shouldn't: 飲まない (ない-form) + 方がいい.

Polite

Your friend is heading out. The sky looks grey.

傘かさ、持もって行いった方ほうがいいよ。

"You should take an umbrella."

Casual

A friend wants to try a new restaurant you already know.

あの店みせは行いかない方ほうがいい。高たかいだけだよ。

"Better not go to that place. It's just expensive."

Casual

Without

早はやく寝ねてください。

"Please go to bed early." A request.

With 方がいい

早はやく寝ねた方ほうがいいですよ。

"You should go to bed early." Advice: it's up to them.

N5 Grammar

～に行く・～に来る

～に行く means go to do something. It answers "going to do what?".

Take the verb's ます-form, drop ます, add に行く: します → しに行く, 食べます → 食べに行く. Activity nouns work too: 買い物に行く, スキーに行く.

With 来る it's "come to do something": 遊びに来る. Polite: に行きます, に来ます. Casual: に行く, に来る.

Examples

You're heading out. You tell your roommate where you're going.

コンビニに飲のみ物ものを買かいに行いくね。

"I'm going to the convenience store to get drinks."

Two に: コンビニに = where, 買いに = to do what.

Casual

Monday at work. A coworker asks about your weekend.

海うみに泳およぎに行いきました。

"I went to the beach for a swim."

泳ぎます → 泳ぎ + に行きました.

Polite

Your friend shows up at your door without warning.

え、何なにしに来きたの？

"Huh, what are you here for?"

Literally "came to do what?". 何しに is a very common question.

Casual

At a party, someone asks why you came to Japan.

日本にほん語ごを勉強べんきょうしに来きました。

"I came to study Japanese."

You're in Japan now, so it's 来る, not 行く.

Polite

With and without

Without

図書としょ館かんに行いきます。

"I'm going to the library." Only where.

With ～に行く

図書としょ館かんに本ほんを返かえしに行いきます。

"I'm going to the library to return a book." Where, and what for.

N5 Grammar

～な (Don't)

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 11

串くしごと食くうなよ。

"Don't eat the skewer too." [the stick and all]

な after a verb means don't: a short, blunt order not to do something.

It goes straight after the dictionary form, nothing changes: 食う → 食うな, する → するな. On this card, it answers "what must I not do?": eat the stick.

It's rough, so you hear it between friends, from parents, on signs and in anime. The よ softens it a little. The polite way to say don't is ないでください.

Examples

Your friend is about to give up on the last kilometer of a run.

諦あきらめるな！

"Don't give up!"

諦める ("give up") + な = "don't give up!". Dictionary form + な: a blunt "don't".

Casual

Your friend is nervous before a job interview.

心配しんぱいするなよ。大丈夫だいじょうぶだって。

"Don't worry. You'll be fine."

する → するな. The よ makes it friendlier.

Casual

You're about to tell everyone your friend's secret.

言いうな！

"Don't say it!"

Casual

A kid runs along the edge of the pool. The lifeguard shouts.

走はしるな！

"No running!"

Casual

A sign next to a river.

ゴミを捨すてるな

"Don't dump trash."

Signs use な because it's short and firm.

Casual

Watch out: not every な at the end is "don't". You step outside in winter.

今日きょうは寒さむいな。

"Man, it's cold today."

After an adjective, な is just a feeling, like "huh" or "man". "Don't" only comes after a verb, said like an order.

Casual

With and without

Without

それ、食たべる？

"Are you going to eat that?" Just asking.

With な

それ、食たべるな！

"Don't eat that!" You're stopping them.

N5 Grammar

て-Form

Polite

YouTube · video

今日きょうはめがねをはずして、コンタクトレンズをつけています。

"Today I took off my glasses and I'm wearing contacts."

The て-form is the verb shape that ends in て or で. On this card, はずす (take off) becomes はずして, and the sentence keeps going.

Make it like the past form, just swap た for て: はずした → はずして, 食べた → 食べて, 飲んだ → 飲んで. If you can say the past, you can say the て-form.

On its own it means "and" between actions. Lots of grammar sits on it: てください (please), ている (is doing), てから (after).

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 12

もっと食たべて。

"Eat more."

The て-form alone is a casual request. On this card, 食べる ("eat") → 食べて, with もっと ("more") in front.

Examples

る-verbs: drop る, add て.

朝あさご飯はんを食たべて、学校がっこうに行いきます。

"I eat breakfast and go to school."

食べる → 食べて. 見る → 見て, 寝る → 寝て.

Polite

Verbs ending in う, つ, る: っ + て.

ちょっと待まって！

"Wait a sec!"

待つ → 待って. 買う → 買って, 帰る → 帰って.

Casual

Verbs ending in む, ぶ, ぬ: ん + で.

この薬くすりを飲のんでください。

"Please take this medicine."

飲む → 飲んで. 遊ぶ → 遊んで, 死ぬ → 死んで.

Polite

Verbs ending in く: い + て.

名前なまえを書かいてください。

"Please write your name."

書く → 書いて. One odd one: 行く → 行って.

Polite

Verbs ending in ぐ: い + で.

急いそいで！電車でんしゃが来くるよ。

"Hurry! The train's coming."

急ぐ → 急いで. 泳ぐ → 泳いで.

Casual

Verbs ending in す: し + て.

もっとゆっくり話はなしてください。

"Please speak more slowly."

話す → 話して. 出す → 出して.

Polite

The two irregular ones.

明日あした、八はち時じに来きてください。

"Please come at eight tomorrow."

来る → 来て, する → して.

Polite

With and without

Without

本ほんを読よんだ。

"I read the book." Past, the sentence ends here.

With て

本ほんを読よんで、寝ねました。

"I read the book and went to sleep." Same shape with で instead of だ, and it keeps going.

N5 Grammar

～て (And then)

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 2

朝あさ起おきて一番いちばんに、中庭なかにわに集あつまって、家族かぞくみんなで太極たいきょく拳けんをします。

"First thing after we get up, we gather in the courtyard and the whole family does tai chi." [Panda talking about home]

て joins actions in the order they happen: get up, gather, do tai chi.

Put each verb in the て-form and keep going: 起きる → 起きて, 集まる → 集まって. Only the last verb shows the tense and the politeness, here します.

So you never need ます in the middle. To make it casual, change only the end: する instead of します.

Casual

ReLIFE · Episode 8

合格ごうかくして 部活ぶかつ行いったよ。

"She passed and went to practice."

The て-form links actions in order, and only the last verb shows the past. On this card, 合格する ("pass") → 合格して + 部活行った ("went to club").

Examples

Your friend asks about your evening.

家いえに帰かえって、シャワーを浴あびて、寝ねました。

"I went home, showered and went to bed."

Past only at the end: 寝ました. The て verbs are past too.

Polite

Telling a friend your plan for Sunday.

渋谷しぶやに行いって、映画えいがを見みる。

"I'll go to Shibuya and watch a movie."

行く → 行って (the odd one).

Casual

Explaining the way to the station.

まっすぐ行いって、二ふたつ目めの角かどを右みぎに曲まがってください。

"Go straight, then turn right at the second corner."

The last verb has てください, so the whole thing is a request.

Polite

Cooking with a friend.

玉たまねぎを切きって、炒いためて。

"Cut the onion and fry it."

切る → 切って. 炒める → 炒めて.

Casual

With and without

Without

家いえに帰かえります。ご飯はんを食たべます。

"I go home. I eat." Two separate sentences.

With て

家いえに帰かえって、ご飯はんを食たべます。

"I go home and eat." One sentence, one action after the other.

パンダくんに聞きいて作つくってみました。

"I asked Panda, then tried making it."

First one thing, then the next.

Casual

Mob Psycho 100 · Episode 8

回収かいしゅうして 帰かえる。

"I'll pick him up and go home."

回収する ("collect, pick up") → 回収して + 帰る ("go home") = "pick him up and go home".

Casual

From the New World · Episode 6

さっさと片かたをつけて 家いえに帰かえるぞ。

"Let's finish this fast and go home."

片をつける ("settle it") → つけて + 家に帰る ("go home") = "finish this and go home". さっさと: "quickly".

Tae Kim's Guide to Japanese Grammar

Compound Sentences · A sequence of verbs with the te-form

N5 Grammar

～くて・～で

Polite

YouTube · video

この辺へんは緑みどりが多おおくて、きれいです。

"This area has lots of green, and it's pretty."

くて joins an い-adjective to what comes next, like "and": lots of green, and pretty.

Drop the last い and add くて: 多い → 多くて, 安い → 安くて. One odd one: いい → よくて.

For な-adjectives and nouns, use で instead: 静かで, 学生で. Only the end shows the politeness: です or nothing.

Casual

Overprotected Kahoko · Episode 3

性格せいかくは優やさしくて 頭あたまが良よくて

"Kind, and smart..."

くて joins an い-adjective to what comes next. On this card, 優しい ("kind") → 優しくて, and いい ("good") → よくて, with 頭がいい = "smart".

Examples

Your friend asks about the new ramen place.

安やすくて、おいしいよ。

"It's cheap and tasty."

安い → 安くて.

Casual

Describing your new apartment.

部屋へやは静しずかで、きれいです。

"The room is quiet and clean."

静か is a な-adjective, so で.

Polite

Introducing yourself.

私わたしは学生がくせいで、二十にじゅう歳さいです。

"I'm a student and I'm twenty."

学生 is a noun, so で.

Polite

Talking about a café.

雰囲気ふんいきがよくて、よく行いくんだ。

"The vibe is nice, so I go there a lot."

いい → よくて. Here it also gives the reason.

Casual

With and without

Without

このラーメンは安やすいです。おいしいです。

"This ramen is cheap. It's tasty." Two separate sentences.

With くて

このラーメンは安やすくて、おいしいです。

"This ramen is cheap and tasty." One smooth sentence.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

甘あまいものが好すきで、もちもちのパンが好すきな人ひとは絶対ぜったいみんな好すきですから。

"Anyone who likes sweet things and chewy bread will love it."

好き is a な-adjective, so で.

Polite

Source unknown No source

美容びよう師しさんは話はなしやすくて、親したしみやすい人ひとが多おおいと思おもいます。

"I think a lot of hairdressers are easy to talk to and friendly."

話しやすい (easy to talk to) → 話しやすくて.

Casual

YouTube · video

なんか静しずかで、なんかちょっと治安ちあんも良よさそう。

"It's kind of quiet, and it seems pretty safe too."

静か is a な-adjective, so で.

Casual

Source unknown No source

オリオン座ざの赤あかくて大おおきい星ほし…

"The big red star in Orion..."

赤い → 赤くて: "red and big".

Casual

Weakest Beast · Episode 5

優やさしくて 責任せきにん感かんが強つよくて

"He was kind and responsible."

優しい ("kind") → 優しくて, 強い ("strong") → 強くて. 責任感が強い = "responsible".

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 20

冷つめたくて気持きもちいい。

"It's cold and feels great."

冷たい drops い, adds くて.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 25

怖こわくて悪わるかったな。

"Sorry for being scary."

Here くて gives the reason.

Entry "-te" · pp. 464–467

Tae Kim's Guide to Japanese Grammar

Compound Sentences · Expressing a sequence of states

N5 Grammar

～てください

Polite～てください
Casual～て

Same meaning: "please do". Only the politeness changes.

Polite

1 Litre of Tears · Episode 1

受験じゅけん生せいは、急いそいでください。

"Exam takers, please hurry." [a staff member at the exam building]

てください after a verb means please do it: you ask someone to do something.

It goes on the て-form. Make it like the past form, just with て instead of た: 急いだ → 急いで, 食べた → 食べて, 行った → 行って. On this card, it answers "what do you want me to do?": hurry.

ください makes it polite: for strangers, shops, teachers. With friends you drop it and just say the て-form.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 14

大丈夫だいじょうぶ、任まかせて。

"It's fine, leave it to me."

Same request, just the て-form with nothing after it. 任せる → 任せて: "leave it (to me)".

Examples

In a shop, you point at a bag behind the counter.

そのかばんを見みせてください。

"Please show me that bag."

見せる → 見せて.

Polite

You get into a taxi.

駅えきまで行いってください。

"To the station, please."

行く → 行って. Literally "please go to the station".

Polite

The teacher spoke too fast and you missed it.

もう一いち度ど言いってください。

"Could you say that again, please?"

言う → 言って.

Polite

Your friend is walking off and you still need your shoes on.

ちょっと待まって！

"Wait a sec!"

待つ → 待って.

Casual

Your friend is busy right now.

じゃあ、あとで電話でんわしてね。

"Okay, call me later."

する → して. The ね makes it softer.

Casual

With and without

Without

窓まどを開あけます。

"I'll open the window." You do it yourself.

With てください

窓まどを開あけてください。

"Please open the window." You ask someone else to do it.

Sentence mining

Polite

YouTube · video

じゃあ、皆みなさん当あててください！

"Okay everyone, take a guess!"

当てる (to guess right) → 当てて.

Polite

YouTube · video

皆みなさんのおすすめのレストランを、ぜひコメント欄らんで教おしえてください！

"Please tell me your favorite restaurants in the comments!"

教える → 教えて. ぜひ adds "really, do".

Polite

積乱せきらん雲くもを見みたら、安全あんぜんな場所ばしょに逃にげてください。

"If you see a thundercloud, get to a safe place."

逃げる → 逃げて.

Polite

YouTube · My Five Favorite Things

詳くわしくは、ウェブサイトをチェックしてください。

"For details, check the website."

チェックする → チェックして.

Casual

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 2

戻もどしてね。

"Put it back, okay?"

戻す ("put back") → 戻して + ね = "put it back, okay?".

Casual

NHK News Web Easy · article

熊くまから自分じぶんを守まもるスプレー、使つかい方かたに気きをつけて。

"Bear spray: be careful how you use it."

気をつける → 気をつけて. A headline, so it's short like casual speech.

Casual

I'm Taking the Day Off · Episode 3

こっち見みて

"Look at me."

Casual request: just the て-form, no ください.

Casual

待まって～！

"Wait for me!"

待つ → 待って: a casual "please wait".

Making Requests · 「～ください」

N5 Grammar

～ないでください

Polite～ないでください
Casual～ないで

Same meaning: "please don't". Only the politeness changes.

Polite

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 4

ドライブスルーで遊あそばないでください。

"Please don't mess around in the drive-thru." [staff talking to customers]

ないでください after a verb means please don't: you ask someone not to do something.

It goes on the ない-form: 遊ぶ → 遊ばない → 遊ばないでください. If you can say "not", just add でください.

ください makes it polite: for strangers, customers, teachers. With friends you drop it and just say ないで.

Casual

YouTube · video

無理むりしないでね。

"Don't push yourself too hard."

Same request without ください. する → しない → しないで. The ね makes it warm.

Examples

In a museum, a kid reaches for a statue.

触さわらないでください。

"Please don't touch."

触る → 触らない.

Polite

Your friend is about to tell everyone your secret.

言いわないで！

"Don't tell!"

言う → 言わない.

Casual

A sign at the pool.

ここで走はしらないでください。

"Please don't run here."

走る → 走らない.

Polite

Your friend says they'll leave you behind.

置おいていかないでよ。

"Don't leave me behind!"

行く → 行かない.

Casual

With and without

Without

写真しゃしんを撮とってください。

"Please take a photo." Asking someone to do it.

With ないでください

写真しゃしんを撮とらないでください。

"Please don't take photos." Asking someone not to.

Source unknown No source

もう二に度どと、うちのクマに関かかわらないでください。

"Please never go near my bear again."

関わる (to get involved with) → 関わらない.

Polite

Source unknown No source

自分じぶんのことを過小かしょう評価ひょうかしないでください。

"Please don't sell yourself short."

過小評価する (to underrate) → しない.

Polite

Source unknown No source

私わたしが集あつめているＣＤのジャケットを、勝手かってに触さわらないでください。

"Please don't touch the CD covers I collect without asking."

触る → 触らない.

Polite

Quartet · Episode 9

もう 謝あやまらないでください。

"Please stop apologizing."

謝る ("apologize") → 謝らない + でください = "please don't apologize". もう: "anymore".

Shirokuma Cafe · Episode 18

"Please don't ask."

ない-form + でください.

Casual

行く ("go") → 行かない + で = "don't go". Casual: no ください.

泣く ("cry") → 泣かない + で = "don't cry". もう: "anymore".
